item.title: 28 states approve State Police Bill as NASS moves to transmit to Tinubu
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The National Assembly has received approval from 28 State Houses of Assembly for the proposed constitutional amendment seeking to establish state police in Nigeria. The approval exceeds the constitutionally required threshold of 24 states, representing two-thirds of the 36 State Houses of Assembly, paving the way for the transmission of the bill to President Bola Tinubu for assent. The Clerk to the National Assembly, Kamoru Ogunlana, disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday, saying the reports received from the 28 state legislatures had been verified alongside their respective votes and proceedings. According to the statement, the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (Sixth Alteration) Bill, which seeks to provide for the establishment of State Police Services and related matters, was transmitted to the 36 State Houses of Assembly on September 16, 2026, for consideration and approval. The state legislatures were initially given 30 days, ending October 15, to communicate their decisions to the National Assembly. However, Ogunlana said his office would continue to receive reports from the state assemblies until the bill is transmitted for presidential assent. He said, “Following the receipt and verification of the reports, the Office confirms that 28 State Houses of Assembly have approved the Bill. “This represents more than the constitutionally prescribed threshold of not less than two-thirds of the 36 State Houses of Assembly, equivalent to 24 States, as required under Section 9 of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999.” The clerk explained that the National Assembly had undertaken administrative verification of the reports and accompanying votes and proceedings to establish their authenticity and ensure that they accurately reflected the decisions taken by the respective state legislatures. He also clarified that Section 9 of the Constitution does not expressly prescribe a third reading for a Constitution Alteration Bill, unlike the procedure applicable to ordinary bills. The post 28 states approve State Police Bill as NASS moves to transmit to Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: The Moments that Made the 2026 Red Sox: Brayan Bello fell back in love with the game
item.description: ST PETERSBURG, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 19: Brayan Bello #66 of the Boston Red Sox reacts with Pitching Coach Andrew Bailey #53 of the Boston Red Sox in the dugout after the eighth inning of a game against the Tampa Bay Rays on September 19, 2026 at at Tropicana Field in St Petersburg, Florida. (Photo by Maddie Malhotra/Boston Red Sox/Getty Images) | Getty Images Something had to give with Brayan Bello in the early days of summer. After a handful of bad starts throughout the first few months of the year were interspersed with a few strong bulk appearances out of the bullpen, the right-handed pitcher absolutely imploded during a rubber game on Thursday, June 4, at Fenway Park. The Baltimore Orioles immediately jumped on him for a six pack of earned runs in the first inning. Bello eventually coughed up another pair of runs—both earned—to end with a line of seven hits and three walks surrendered across five frames. He hit one guy with a pitch, too, in case you needed any extra convincing as to how bad of a game it was for number 66. It was the straw (or, I suppose group of eight straws?) that broke the camel’s back. Bello’s ERA on the year had ballooned to 6.34 across 61 innings following that loss to the O’s, which was actually the second instance in the first half where Baltimore charged him for eight earned. He wasn’t working deep enough into games, and he had made his frustrations with that fact clear on at least one public occasion . He was adamant that his struggles as a starter (and his relative successes as a reliever) were not indicative of any trends, per The Athletic . “First of all, just stop talking about bullpen and starting games. I’ve always been a starter, and when I’ve been successful as a starter, no one asks your question (about) whether I have to be in the bullpen or starting games. So, just starting from there, just stop that talk, because I’m just having a bad season…I know that I can turn it around.” Not exactly the type of stuff you want to see or hear from the guy who figured to be playing an important role in your pennant aspirations, as evidenced by the eight-figure deal that he was given a few years ago. CBO Craig Breslow must’ve agreed, because he made a drastic decision soon after the most recent Bello blowup: the 27-year-old was being sent back down to the minors. As he explained via MassLive … “But one of the things that we messaged to him was, when I first got here, he was a guy who had this big personality. He always had a smile on his face, interacting with his teammates and you could tell loved to compete and loved to pitch. And I think we’ve lost that a little bit where he was putting a ton of pressure on himself go out and perform. So one of the things we asked him to do was to fall in love with baseball all over again —to go down, to compete. But to kind of remember why he loved playing this game.” As we all know by now, that trip to and from Worcester must’ve ironed something out in Bello’s game. He came back with

item.title: Monday Night Therapy: Husker Fans, We Need to Talk
item.description: Three straight losses. Three fourth quarter collapses. Three games where Nebraska looked like the better team for three quarters, only to watch another victory slip away. After heartbreaking losses to Indiana and Oregon, Saturdays collapse against Washington has Husker Nation at a breaking point!! Questionable decisions by the quarterback, receivers not getting open, frustrating play calling and another late game meltdown have Husker fans demanding answers. Why isn’t Nebraska able to score? item.title: Offensive Coordinator targets for the Oklahoma Sooners
item.description: The first casualty of a disappointing 2026 season for the Oklahoma Sooners was announced on Monday morning when Oklahoma moved on from offensive coordinator/quarterbacks coach Ben Arbuckle after less than two seasons with the team. Tight ends coach Jason Witten will serve as interim offensive coordinator and play-caller for the rest of the season. Arbuckle and quarterback John Mateer helped the offense take a slight step forward in 2025, as the Sooners made the College Football Playoff. However, the offense took major steps in the wrong direction this year, and now Arbuckle's short time in Norman is over . With Mateer out of eligibility after this season, Oklahoma will have a new-look offense in 2027. The OU offense is in Witten's hands for the rest of this year, but the Sooners are set to have another offensive coordinator search under Venables. Simply put, Venables has to get this hire right. We're going to exclude the potential hires that aren't overly realistic, such as Florida offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner or Texas State head coach G.J. Kinne. This list includes a variety of coaches with different backgrounds, but ultimately it's up to Venables to make the hire, which will likely happen in about a month. Here are several candidates who could be a good fit. Chip Kelly, Northwestern Offensive Coordinator Northwestern offensive coordinator Chip Kelly probably checks the most boxes in terms of what OU is (hopefully) looking for. He's a brilliant offensive mind who has been the head coach at Oregon (2009-2012) and UCLA (2018-2023) and also in the NFL with the Philadelphia Eagles (2013-2015) and San Francisco 49ers (2016). Before he was coaching the Ducks, he was the OC at New Hampshire (1999-2006), before later landing the same gig in Eugene (2007-2008). Then, he was promoted to head coach, where he rose to fame. More recently, he was the OC for Ohio State in 2024, and for the Las Vegas Raiders in 2025. He landed at Northwestern this year and is helping the Wildcats to a strong season in 2026. He's got plenty of experience, and he would not let things fall apart at OU on offense. He can also run a variety of offensive schemes, and he tailors it to what his team needs. Kelly wouldn't be the "Oklahoma" hire, but maybe that's what the Sooners need. He's got an interesting past and isn't interested in recruiting, but he'd be a candidate who could get results on Saturdays. Mitch Dahlen, Oregon State Offensive Coordinator Oregon State offensive coordinator Mitch Dahlen would represent a different direction than Kelly. He's far less experienced, and he's coaching in the Pac-12 instead of a Power Four league, but his offense has been lethal this season, led by star quarterback Braden Atkinson. Dahlen knows how to coach quarterbacks, and he's followed Alabama head coach Kalen DeBoer around from Fresno State to Washington to Tuscaloosa, before going out on his own this season. He's working under head coach JaMarcus Shephard, another DeBoer disciple

item.title: CDS seeks civilian support, intelligence sharing to tackle terrorism
item.description: The Chief of Defence Staff, Gen. Olufemi Oluyede, has called for the support of civilians and host communities in the fight against terrorism. Oluyede made the call while speaking to newsmen on the sidelines of the 2026 Chief of Naval Staff (CNS) annual retreat on Tuesday in Abuja. According to Oluyede, there is a need for jointness and synergy among all key security stakeholders. Oluyede, whose philosophy for security lays heavy emphasis on synergy, said that jointness goes beyond inter-agency cooperation and also includes the civilians and communities. “It is important for us to continue to emphasise jointness because no single service can do the job alone, it requires a collective effort.” He said the armed forces are collectively doing their very best to make Nigeria safer, adding that what they require from Nigerians are support, prayers and intelligence reports. “If you see anything, you should tell us because everything we’re doing relies on intelligence, and for that, we need community support,” he said. He said the support provided by Nigerians would aid push the country forward on all fronts. He assured Nigerians that things would continue to get better. (NAN) The post CDS seeks civilian support, intelligence sharing to tackle terrorism appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Shaw among big names to miss out on FifPro World XI
item.description: Manchester City stars Khadija Shaw (left) and Lauren Hemp (right) missed out [Getty Images] Eyebrows were raised on Monday when the FifPro Women's World XI shortlist was unveiled and several big names were missing. The 26-player shortlist was voted for by players from around the world and is the only award decided solely by fellow footballers. It is considered prestigious as a result but when the list dropped and five of the top 10 Ballon d'Or finishers were not included, it understandably caused a stir. Among the notable absentees was Manchester City's top scorer Khadija Shaw, who finished third in the Ballon d'Or. Malawi star Temwa Chawinga and Haiti's Melchie Dumornay were also shock omissions, along with Barcelona's Caroline Graham Hansen and Denmark captain Pernille Harder. However, England trio Ella Toone, Chloe Kelly and Aggie Beever-Jones are surprise inclusions. Find interviews and extra content on the BBC Women's Football Weekly feed How does the voting work? The world XI shortlist was voted for by 6,511 women's footballers from 64 countries via an online system with FifPro. The finalists are the players who received the most votes judged on their period between 4 August 2025 and 16 August 2026. All players had to feature at least 20 times during that period to be eligible for nomination and the winners will be unveiled on Monday, 9 November (13:00 GMT). The world XI will consist of one goalkeeper, three defenders, three midfielders and three forwards who all received the most votes in their positions. The remaining spot will be taken by the outfield player, from any position, with the next highest number of votes. Votes for a player in more than one position (for example, if they are named as a midfielder or a forward), are combined. Which nominations were controversial? It is not the first time the shortlists have been controversial. Last year, Arsenal and Spain midfielder Mariona Caldentey was not included in the FifPro World XI despite coming runner-up in the Ballon d'Or. In 2024, when 7,000 women's footballers voted, four of the top five in the Ballon d'Or were not shortlisted, including the often overlooked Graham Hansen. Instead, five Lionesses made the cut despite not winning a major trophy that year or having any finalists in the Ballon d'Or top 10. This time around the WSL's Player of the Year Shaw missed out. She helped Manchester City win a league and FA Cup double as their top scorer with 21 goals in 22 games. Meanwhile, the inclusions of England trio Toone, Kelly and Beever-Jones were controversial with all three initially failing to make the most recent Lionesses squad. Chelsea's Beever-Jones scored just seven goals in all competitions for club and country during the period of voting, while Toone and Kelly both struggled for form and fitness in that time. item.title: Has Georges Mikautadze made come-and-get-me plea to Barcelona?
item.description: Has Georges Mikautadze made come-and-get-me plea to Barcelona? Georges Mikautadze (26) was the subject of interest from Barcelona last summer. The Georgian centre-forward had excelled during his first season at Villarreal, following a summer move from Olympique Lyonnais, netting 16 goals in 44 appearances in all competitions. Barcelona’s sporting director Deco scrutinised Mikautadze, but following conversations with manager Hansi Flick, their interest did not go any further. Mikautadze’s start to this season has been more difficult. Despite netting five goals in all competitions, he has made just five starts in La Liga so far. The striker has admitted to L’Équipe that he is “disappointed” by the situation. However, he added that he still feels as though he is “ready to go to a big club”. Mikautadze also specifically referenced Barcelona’s interest in the summer and revealed that he is a fan of the Catalan giants. “The Barcelona interest? It is flattering and it motivates me even more. It also means that the work is done well. On top of that, since the Xavi-Iniesta-Busquets and the MSN (Messi-Suarez-Neymar), I have been a Barca fan […] but I didn’t think too much about that ,” he told the French publication ahead of Villarreal’s UEFA Champions League game against Paris Saint-Germain. Mikautadze would naturally not be opposed to a move to the Camp Nou; it is a question of whether Barcelona revive their interest and whether Flick can be convinced. GSFN | Luke Entwistle

item.title: Milwaukee Brewers: Jacob Misiorowski competition for 2026 NL Cy Young revealed
item.description: Back in 2025, the Milwaukee Brewers made the decision to promote their top pitching prospect, Jacob Misiorowsk i, to the Major League level. This move led one former Brewers pitcher, Aaron Civale, to demand a trade as he was going to lose his spot in the starting rotation. Since then, Misiorowski has made two All-Star rosters, set multiple pitch velocity records, became the ace of the staff, and won the World Series. Civale has played for three different teams, primarily as a reliever. Oh, and Civale netted Milwaukee first baseman Andrew Vaughn. Milwaukee Brewers ace Jacob Misiorowski is a NL Cy Young finalist Aug 21, 2026; Milwaukee, Wisconsin, USA; Milwaukee Brewers starting pitcher Jacob Misiorowski (32) throws a pitch in the first inning against the Atlanta Braves at American Family Field. Mandatory Credit: Benny Sieu-Imagn Images Late in the 2025 season, though, the Brewers had to move Misiorowski to the bullpen. He was becoming fatigued as he pitched deeper into the season than he had ever done, and his pitches were not moving as well. Despite this move, Misiorowski performed well in the 2025 postseason. However, many wondered if he would be able to build up the endurance needed to start over the course of an entire Major League season. He began the 2026 season as the ace of Milwaukee’s staff and soon proved to everyone that not only could he make a full season’s worth of starts, he would be one of the best pitchers in the game while doing it. Now, he is the favorite to win the NL Cy Young Award, a notion made official when the finalist were announced on Monday night: Your 2026 @officialBBWAA NL Cy Young Award finalists: Jacob Misiorowski, Brewers Chris Sale, Braves Cristopher Sánchez, Phillies https://t.co/SY9wgVugvX — MLB (@MLB) November 3, 2026 Misiorowski finished the regular season 16-5 with a 1.80 ERA (led the Majors), 252 strikeouts (led the Majors), 0.80 WHIP (led the Majors), and .157 opponent batting average (the best of all time). Chris Sale and Cristopher Sanchez have been in the Cy Young conversation all season long, but the last few months have seen the Brewers ace pull away from them. At this point, it is Misiorowski’s award to win and a two-man race for second place. item.title: Fantasy football waiver wire Week 9: Emmett Johnson, Adonai Mitchell finally pay off
item.description: Not wrong, just early. That’s what we’re hoping is the case for our Emmett Johnson and Jonah Coleman sleeper picks. The two rookie Day 3 draft picks showed out in Sunday’s battle between the Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos . Each had more than 100 yards from scrimmage. Each had at least four catches. Each found the end zone, with Coleman setting up the game-winning score on a 52-yard catch-and-run, then crashing over the goal line one play later. We were high on the pair back in the preseason , only to get little in return. Johnson was a non-factor after a disappointing Week 1. Coleman seemed to take a key role in the Broncos ’ tailback rotation before a Week 2 injury took him off the field and left him to prove himself all over again. Now they look like potential season savers – but since we’ve talked about Coleman a lot lately , let’s zoom in on Johnson’s role going forward and where belongs on your roster. And, because we’re leaning into repeats this week, let’s talk about Adonai Mitchell’s latest revival as well. I'm joined by fantasy expert and Rhode Island Scumbag Mike "Yaj" Boyajian to break down the players who’ll be thrust into a larger role in Week 9, either thanks to their own skill or an opportunity created by departures elsewhere on the depth chart. We'll talk about those players, as well as the guys rostered around their level and reasonably higher, to figure out if you should add Johnson or Mitchell to your rosters -- and who you should drop to bring them aboard. The rules? There's pretty much only one; players have to be 33 percent owned or less in Yahoo! fantasy football leagues. Who's going to spark a bidding war on your waiver wire this week – and who should you drop to pick him up? RB Emmett Johnson, Kansas City Chiefs (19 percent owned in Yahoo! leagues) Johnson had his long awaited breakthrough, serving as the most effective option in the Kansas City passing game in Week 8. Even if 73 yards came on a jailbreak run-after-catch, he turned four other targets into 55 yards and showed off elusive running skills with his lone carry. His place in the backfield is a bit uneven with Kenneth Walker III ahead of him but coming off two inefficient weeks. Does that make Johnson a better roster option than… Dylan Sampson, Cleveland Browns (17 percent owned) Christian: Take Johnson . Sampson has plenty of PPR utility, but the Cleveland passing game is a mess and that utility will disappear if he gets a quarterback interested in pushing the ball downfield. That’s not Deshaun Watson, formerly accused of more than 20 counts of sexual misconduct and what an NFL investigation deemed “predatory behavior,” who targeted him six times, most of which came in the second half of a division rivalry game the Browns trailed by multiple possessions after the break. item.title: NFL Power Rankings Week 9: Hilarious Cowboys can’t even be saved by another blockbuster trade
item.description: Ah, November. The time of year when leaves turn crisp, rain turns freezing, and we start separating pretenders and contenders in the context of an NFL season. The 2026 campaign is no different. Even with Bo Nix’s Jekyll and Hyde play, his Denver Broncos somehow sit at the top of the AFC West. The Cincinnati Bengals , meanwhile, are receiving MVP play from Joe Burrow, but seem to have the same defensive issues that have plagued them since their run to Super Bowl 56. In the NFC, until or if they can find a better quarterback than Kyler Murray, it’s really hard to take the Minnesota Vikings seriously. On the flip side, if the Green Bay Packers can piece together a functional running game, they appear capable of making a lot of noise this coming winter. Then there’s the Dallas Cowboys . The Cowboys, as ever, remain a cursed franchise dedicated to inventing new ways to pull defeat out of the jaws of victory every single week. It’s to the point where we’re pretty sure another monster trade wouldn’t even fix what ails Dallas because their problems run much deeper. That might not stop Jerry Jones from making one, though. But what else is new? Let’s unpack all the latest shifts in the landscape of the 2026 NFL season in For The Win’s Week 9 NFL Power Rankings. 32. Los Angeles Chargers Last week: 32 Jim Harbaugh's offense is a bowling pin setter. An unremarkable piece of old-school machinery that does its job in a way you don't truly appreciate. Mike McDaniel came in and replaced all his bowling pins with early 90s troll dolls, and now the whole operation is failing as two incongruent systems crash into each other week after week. All the Chargers have to offer in 2026 is schadenfreude. — Christian D'Andrea 31. New York Jets Last week: 30 Do you know how hard it is to lose against a West Coast team playing an early-afternoon East Coast game? Aaron Glenn's Jets, everyone! The rebuild he insists is going swimmingly is actually going, well, like any other recent Jets rebuild. That is to say, it's going bad. Very bad. — Robert Zeglinski 30. Miami Dolphins Last week: 29 Malik Willis has stacked back-to-back efficient performances, suggesting he could be turning a corner as he builds rapport with a young playmaking corps still adjusting to the loss of De'Von Achane, the team's only proven veteran engine. Expectations are modest, but he's shown he deserves a chance to run this offense with a roster that isn't dedicating 40 percent of its salary cap space to players who aren't even on the team. — CD 29. Philadelphia Eagles Last week: 26 There's no way the Eagles can let Nick Sirianni keep his job just because of their rash of injury issues this year. This is a poorly coached, undisciplined team that makes self-inflicted mistakes every week, without fail. If anything, the Eagles should take the possible top-five draft pick that will come from this cursed season and gift it to a new coach with a more coherent vision for the organization in the offseason. — RZ 28. item.title: ‘Are You Even Listening?’ ‘He’s Been Extremely Complimentary’ — NFL Fans Call Out Claims of Troy Aikman Being Biased Against Bears QB Caleb Williams
item.description: ‘Are You Even Listening?’ ‘He’s Been Extremely Complimentary’ — NFL Fans Call Out Claims of Troy Aikman Being Biased Against Bears QB Caleb Williams Some Chicago Bears fans were listening to Troy Aikman as closely as they were watching Caleb Williams in a 34-17 win over the Seattle Seahawks on Monday Night Football. It came a little more than a year after his call of a Bears win at Washington set off a public back-and-forth with the Bears quarterback. That revived a perception among some Bears fans that Aikman is unusually critical of Williams (something Aikman has publicly denied). One viewer wasted little time reviving that criticism during the game, accusing Aikman of questioning everything the Bears offense did. But to his surprise, others watching the same broadcast heard a very different Aikman. Year-Old Bias Theory About Troy Aikman Resurfaces on MNF Greg Gabriel, the Bears’ former director of college scouting, wrote ahead of Monday’s game that “Aikman does not like Caleb and has always been negative towards him.” Gabriel speculated that the perceived tension began after Williams and Aikman failed to connect for their usual production meeting before a game against the Commanders in 2025. “Supposedly it started when Caleb missed a production meeting and Aikman took it personally,” he added . That meeting was scheduled for before Chicago’s 25-24 win at Washington on Oct. 13, 2025, but the two never met. Aikman’s critique of Williams that night, including his take on D’Andre Swift’s 55-yard catch-and-run, drew objections from both Williams and coach Ben Johnson. According to Awful Announcing , Aikman told “The Ticket,” a Dallas radio station, that month, “I’m a fan of his; I like the way he plays.” IMPROVE YOUR TEAM: PFN’s Free Fantasy Trade Calculator Monday, Aikman was back on the call for the Bears game, with Williams under center. Early in the first quarter, one fan tried to sound the alarm, writing , “Troy Aikman has questioned literally everything the Bears offense has done so far tonight. I can’t stand this dude.” Fans Push Back After Hearing a Changed Troy Aikman Did everyone hear the same broadcast? You would expect so, but did everyone hear a bitter Aikman taking shots at the Bears and Williams? Not according to those who came to Aikman’s defense, starting with one fan who answered , “Sounded fine to me?” Others also shared his sentiment on the matter and waved off the complaint, writing , “Quit being a drama queen.” PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Two others heard more than a fair call. Another fan wrote , “Honestly, I feel like he has gone out of his way to compliment Caleb, which is a MASSIVE change.” Another fan made the same point, writing , “He’s done a 180. Are you even listening?” Finally, one fan was less diplomatic, asking , “[expletive] are you talking about? He’s been extremely complimentary,” before adding that they had muted the OP for “rage bait.” Whatever the booth made of it, Williams finish

item.title: 'Certainly hasn't impressed me' - Ex-Aston Villa scout questions whether goalkeeper Zion Suzuki justifies £30m fee after Fulham blunder
item.description: Aston Villa FC v Fulham - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Former Aston Villa senior scout Bryan King has questioned whether summer signing Zion Suzuki has done enough to justify his £30 million transfer fee following a costly error against Fulham. The 24-year-old Japan international fumbled a corner into his own net during Saturday's 1-1 Premier League draw despite pulling off several earlier saves. Costly mistake mars positive start Suzuki endured his first major setback in a Villa shirt on Saturday when he dropped an Alex Iwobi corner into his own goal against Fulham. Just minutes before that costly lapse, the former Parma shot-stopper had produced a string of fine interventions, including a point-blank stop to thwart Oscar Bobb. Despite earning widespread acclaim for his reflexes and distribution since arriving in Birmingham, his display drew strong criticism. Former goalkeeper criticises extravagant style Assessing the young custodian's development, former professional goalkeeper King argued that the summer recruit still has plenty to prove as Villa's first-choice option. Speaking to Football Insider , he said: "This is a goalkeeper who makes saves look so much harder than they are, more spectacular than they are. He wants to concentrate on the simple job. He's entitled to have one good save in the game. That usually happens when you're a goalkeeper. Unfortunately, they never remember the good save. Of course he will bounce back if he's got anything about him. But as I say, he's a goalkeeper who certainly hasn't impressed me. Not for the money they paid for him." Casting further doubt over the £30m investment, King added: "I would expect the goalkeeper to come back. If he cost that amount of money, then one mistake shouldn't harm his season. But the jury's still out on him for me." Unai Emery defends Japanese stopper Despite the external scrutiny, Villa supporters and coaching staff rallied around the 24-year-old immediately after the final whistle in recognition of his strong early-season form. Head coach Emery was quick to publicly back his number one and highlight his earlier contributions during the stalemate. Speaking after the match, the Spanish tactician said: "It's part of football. We can identify and we are mature to understand we are making mistakes when we are playing. I as a coach, make mistakes everyday. Players make mistakes every match. One match in the middle of the field is not so relevant but for a goalkeeper, those mistakes are more in focus. But it's part of football and keep going forward. I prefer to speak about the saves he did." Camp Nou test awaits goalkeeper Given Emery's staunch public backing, Suzuki is firmly expected to retain his starting berth between the posts as Villa turn their attention back to European duties. item.title: Every player from Alabama to play for the Boston Celtics - DJ White
item.description: The Boston Celtics have traded for, signed, and drafted players from nearly every U.S. state and countries across the globe. From Alabama to Yugoslavia, the Celtics have a history of thoroughly seeking talent to succeed in the NBA. Since their beginnings in the Basketball Association of America (a precursor league of the NBA) in the earliest years of the Association, the organization has tirelessly searched for talent since its inception. In this installment of our series documenting the origins of every player who has represented the Celtics, we will focus on players from Alabama who have played for Boston. Our focus in this article is DJ White. An alum of Indiana, he was picked up with the 29th overall selection of the 2008 NBA Draft by the Detroit Pistons . The Tuscaloosa, Alabama native played the first 3 seasons of his pro career with the Oklahoma City Thunder instead. He also played for the Charlotte Hornets before he signed with the Boston Celtics in 2013. His stay with the team lasted until he was dealt to the Brooklyn Nets that same year. During his time suiting up for the Celtics, White put up 2.4 points and 1.1 rebounds per game. All stats and data courtesy of Basketball Reference. item.title: Matt Rhule reveals Nebraska fan verbally attacked his daughter
item.description: Credit: KETV NewsWatch 7 The Nebraska Cornhuskers lost their third straight game, falling 17-10 to Washington on Saturday, and head coach Matt Rhule dedicated his Monday press conference to defending his program. Rhule spoke uninterrupted for 19 minutes before opening his presser to questions. In that time, he analyzed what went wrong against Washington, credited individual coaches and players, including offensive coordinator Dana Holgorsen and quarterback Anthony Colandrea, for their effort, and pulled back the curtain on how the college football pressure cooker spilled over into his personal life. NEW: Nebraska HC Matt Rhule says his daughter was verbally assaulted after last week’s game: “A guy walked up to my 13-year-old daughter and was like, “F*** U and F*** your dad.” “I’m not going to keep coaching if it means my kids grow up screwed up. I’m not going to see my daughter shook.” — College Transfer Portal (@CollegeFBPortal) November 2, 2026 “There’s so many people that you do not want to let down,” Rhule said. “I do not want to let the fans down. I don’t want to let our players down, I don’t want to let our coaches down, but I got to go to work. What I will say, though, is this: I’m also going to fight for my family.” “My kids have grown up in coaching—and I say this for all the coaches out there,” Rhule continued. “I love our fans. But a guy walked up to my 13-year-old daughter and was like, ‘F you and F your dad.’ I’m not going to keep coaching if it means my kids grow up screwed up. I’m not going to [keep] coaching to see my daughter shook.” Rhule emphasized that he’s willing to “fight” for the die-hard fans who don’t cross inappropriate boundaries. “The guy that attacked my 13-year-old daughter, I’m not coaching for him,” Rhule said. “I’m coaching for the people that are in the boat. So, you guys can ask me whatever you want, man, but just please don’t question anybody’s integrity or effort.” Rhule doubled down on his commitment to Nebraska and its “passionate” fan base—the “grown man” who harassed his daughter notwithstanding. “I’m not leaving, I’m not quitting, I’m fighting for those people,” he said. Rhule also revealed what his 10-year-old daughter texted him. “She was like, ‘Mom had the question with us, like, is this too much for you guys?'” Rhule said. “She was like, ‘Dad, I love Nebraska, I love living in Nebraska, I love Nebraska football, [and] I love the players. I’m tough. This is just teaching me life lessons. Please don’t quit.’ So, how do you keep the team motivated? You know what I’m going to say to them? Don’t quit.” The Cornhuskers named Rhule their head football coach and signed him to an eight-year contract in November 2022, shortly after the Carolina Panthers fired him . Rhule previously coached Temple and Baylor at the college level. Nebraska is 24-22 under Rhule. Nebraska (5-3) will visit the Illinois Fighting Illini (5-3) on Friday, Nov. 6. item.title: Quinshon Judkins Calls Out Browns Over ‘Self-Inflicted Wounds’
item.description: The Cleveland Browns saw their two-game winning streak end on Sunday, as they fell prey to the Pittsburgh Steelers in lopsided fashion. In the eyes of Cleveland running back Quinshon Judkins, the 27-6 loss of his team can be largely blamed on the Browns themselves. “All the self-inflicted wounds…penalties, false starts, stuff like that that we can really control…even with the field position that we have and with the defense getting their particular field position and them getting a stop and us not being able to execute is definitely frustrating,” Judkins told reporters following the game, via Camryn Justice of News 5 Cleveland . Penalties Hurt Quinshon Judkins, Browns in Week 8 Loss to The Steelers Oct 25, 2026; Nashville, Tennessee, USA; Cleveland running back Judkins (10) runs the ball against the Tennessee Titans during the first half at Nissan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images The Browns were flagged for nine penalties for 85 yards and also committed two turnovers, both fumbles, with Deshaun Watson and tight end Harold Fannin Jr. committing one apiece. Cleveland racked up 319 total yards, but only managed to have 17 first downs, thanks to an inefficient 4/13 showing on third downs and 0/2 on fourth downs. Judkins himself didn’t have a great day, with the former Ohio State Buckeyes star collecting just 25 rushing yards on 11 carries. Through eight weeks, Cleveland still has a lot of adjustments to make in order to be taken more seriously. Field discipline is one the Browns can priorotize, as they are last in the NFL with 0.07 penalties a game. On the season, the Browns are also only 29th in the league with just an average of 17.4 points per game and 17th with a -0.1 turnover margin per game. The 5-3 Browns can bounce back as soon as Sunday, when they share the field with the New Orleans Saints at the Caesars Superdome in New Orleans before heading back home for a Week 10 clash against the Houston Texans. item.title: Do we know how many Starship launches SpaceX will need to get NASA astronauts to the moon? No. Will its refuelling plan be simple? Also no.
item.description: null NASA's Artemis IV moon mission will be a complicated affair — especially if SpaceX's Starship ends up being the lunar lander. For all of the changing components of the Artemis program over the past several years, one of its most persistent may be the question of how many refueling flights Starship will need to land astronauts on the moon . By summer 2021, it was common knowledge that Starship would require multiple launches to pull off an Artemis moon landing. A Government Accountability Office audit at the time, for example, estimated that it could take up to 16. Earlier this month, a member of the Aerospace Safety Advisory Panel said the refueling number could be as high as 22. But that estimate was quickly refuted by SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk , who posted on his social media platform, X, that it would actually be closer to six or eight. Perhaps an even bigger head scratcher, though, is how the refueling process will be carried out. Where (and when) will Starship's upper stage gas up when it's off planet? NASA released a graphic during a recent Artemis update that outlined an order of operations for the spacecraft on Artemis IV , which will be the program's first crewed lunar landing. The mission will launch a Space Launch System (SLS) rocket with the four Artemis IV astronauts aboard NASA's Orion capsule to high Earth orbit, where they will rendezvous and dock with the Starship lunar lander. NASA's Artemis IV mission outline featuring Starship as the lunar lander. (Image credit: NASA) Using Starship's engines, the two spacecraft will burn for the moon, and separate upon their arrival in low lunar orbit. Two astronauts will remain aboard Orion, while the other two will head down to the lunar surface in Starship. After a little run through the regolith and a celebration of America's triumphant return to the moon, the duo will board Starship again to launch back to lunar orbit and dock with Orion before beginning the trip back to Earth . All that seems well and good for a mission to the moon, and even has some resemblances with missions from NASA's Apollo days . What doesn't seem as immediately obvious when mapping out the Artemis IV mission outline, though, are the steps that Starship will be taking during its refueling process before the astronauts ever make it to space . Orion will rendezvous with Starship in high Earth orbit — but that's not where the lander will launch initially. According to NASA's Artemis IV outline, SpaceX will first launch a depot ship to low Earth orbit (LEO), which will serve as the repository for all the fuel the Starship lander will eventually need. The graphic shows a tanker Starship docked with the depot with "(multiple)" written next to it, so we don't know how many refueling flights will be needed for this initial depot fill. Once that's done, SpaceX will launch the Starship lunar lander to join the depot in LEO for its first pit stop. Then, and this is where some of the head scratching begins, Starsh

item.title: NBA scouts missed Yaxel Lendeborg’s greatness with an easy mistake
item.description: (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images The high school class of 2020 produced one of the most hyped collections of top-ranked prospects in recent memory. Jalen Green, Terrence Clarke, and Josh Christopher were household names from early in their teenage years for mixtape compilations that drew comparisons to Kobe Bryant and other star scorers. Jalen Suggs was a two-sport stud who bypassed an Ohio State football scholarship because he was better at basketball. Scottie Barnes and Evan Mobley were portable, long-limbed defensive prodigies, and Cade Cunningham shot up to the top of the class after a stirring EYBL run that had him looking like American Luka Doncic . Yaxel Lendeborg was also in the class of 2020, but while his peers were gracing the cover of SLAM and winning international gold medals, he had yet to play organized basketball. Lendeborg’s grades weren’t good enough to get on the court back in his hometown of Pennsauken, New Jersey, and he was more interested in playing video games than applying himself to anything that would better his future. It’s possible his enormous talent would have slipped through the cracks entirely if not for a junior college on the other side of the country taking a chance on him with its last scholarship in a Covid-shortened season following an impressive weekend at an exposure camp for Dominican players. Nearly six years later, Lendeborg already looks like something close to an NBA star as a 24-year-old rookie with the Golden State Warriors. His winding journey from Arizona Western College to UAB to Michigan to now playing alongside Stephen Curry has no real analog, but it still offers some valuable insight into how prospect evaluation is changing in a rapidly evolving landscape for young players. Lendeborg is an exception to just about every rule in the sport, but his ascent is no accident, and it could inform similar success stories in the coming years for teams looking hard enough. What Lendeborg is doing to open this season is nothing short of amazing. He’s averaging 22.3 points, 7.3 rebounds, and 3.7 assists on pristine 64.5% true shooting through his first seven games. His 37-point explosion against the Los Angeles Clippers on Sunday showed the full extent of his skill set. When he was guarded by the skinnier Derrick Jones Jr., Lendeborg wielded body blows in the paint for easy scoring chances. When Brook Lopez tried to corral him in drop coverage off a pick-and-roll, Lendeborg calmly drained a pull-up three-pointer. He showed impressive body control when attacking downhill, and relentless aggression in punishing a small guard in Darius Garland on switches. With a like-sized defender in Kobe Sanders on him, he ripped mid-range shots like a seasoned pro. No rookie should be capable of this type of immediate excellence. Then again, Lendeborg is anything but a typical rookie. YAXEL LENDEBORG: MOST POINTS BY A WARRIORS ROOKIE IN A SINGLE GAME SINCE STEPH IN 2010! 🌉 37 PTS (career-high, game-high) 🌉

item.title: Greatest Washington Senators: A Twinkie Town Definitive List (Round 2)
item.description: 1924 Washington Senators: Pitcher Walter Johnson. (photo by: HUM Images/ Universal Images Group via Getty Images) R1 : Walter Johnson In the biggest landslide since Ronald Reagan in 1980 , Walter Johnson was voted the greatest Washington Senator of all time. Had this been a poll for “greatest pitcher of all time”, he’d still have gotten votes. Truly one of the all-time greats. Up next: Another fleet-footed, defensive-whiz gamer. Round 2 Sam Rice (1915-1933): 2,889 H, 479 2B, 183 3B, 346 SB, .323 BA, .804 OPS, 113 OPS+, 54.1 bWAR. An outfielder who hit left-handed but threw right-handed, Rice was the ultimate speed-and-contact player for the Senators. After a stint in the U.S. Navy and a stop with the Petersburg Goobers of the Virginia League, he twice led the league in hits, once in stolen bases, and once in three-baggers. His career hit total—2,987—remains the closest to 3k of any retired player without reaching that milestone, a fact that may have kept him out of the HOF until the Veteran’s Committee voted him aboard in 1963. Perhaps best known for a controversial catch in the 1925 World Series . Goose Goslin (1921-1930, 1933, 1938): 1,659 H, 289 2B, 125 3B, 127 HR, 932 RBI, 117 SB, .323 BA, .888 OPS, 131 OPS+, 43.4 bWAR. A farm kid from New Jersey introduced to the sport via town ball, Leon Allen Goslin was given the nickname “Goose” when his penchant for waving his arms while tracking spheres in LF looked waterfowl-ish. Goose ultimately had the last laugh, winning an AL batting crown in 1928 and taking home the RBI distinction in 1924. His game was a mix of powerful contact and a little speed—twice leading the circuit in dashes to 3B. Four times he finished top-10 in AL MVP voting, and his six consecutive hits in the 1924 World Series helped the Senators nab their first title. The HOF Veteran’s Committee inducted him in 1968. A year later, severe abdominal burns from falling asleep on his couch while smoking a cigar led to Goslin’s larynx being removed and his death in 1971. Joe Judge (1915-1932): 2,291 H, 421 2B, 157 3B, 210 SB, .299 BA, .802 OPS, 115 OPS+, 48.3 bWAR. As a batsman, Judge was functional and fleet. But in an era known for shoddy defense with bad baseballs and awkward hand-wear, Judge was a consummate glove-man at the first sack. At retirement, he led the American League in fielding percentage, putouts, assists, total chances, & double plays. The kid from Brooklyn—discovered by his block’s postal worker, who gave young Joe his first glove— preserved Walter Johnson’s only MLB no-hitter with a fantastic snare for the final out in 1920. Ironically, he effectively ended the Big Train’s career in 1927 when he smashed a BP bottle-rocket into the hurler’s shin and broke his ankle. Judge died at the age of 68 in 1963 while shoveling snow outside of his D.C. home. Buddy Myer (1925-1927, 1929-1941): 1,828 H, 305 2B, 113 3B, 118 SB, .303 BA, .801 OPS, 109 OPS+, 42.3 bWAR. A college baseball star at Mississippi State, Myer was the Nick Pun

item.title: Grant Wolfram was fine for the Orioles
item.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 25: Grant Wolfram #48 of the Baltimore Orioles throws a pitch during the seventh inning against the New York Yankees in game two of a double-header at Yankee Stadium on September 25, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images) | Getty Images Grant Wolfram came to the Orioles in April 2025 in a minor trade with the Milwaukee Brewers. He made his Major League debut at that month at the age of 28. He ultimately appeared in 21 games for the Orioles over three separate stints. He ended the year with a 5.40 ERA and mostly seemed like the kind of pitcher we didn’t need to pay much attention to. Then he made the 2026 Opening Day roster and somehow became a fixture in the team’s bullpen. He spent the entire season with the big league club and made 60 appearances, becoming a go-to lefty with the loss of Keegan Akin to injury. And while his overall numbers (4.30 ERA, 1.318 WHIP) were underwhelming, to say the least, he was a pitcher that had runs of effectiveness over the season. The funny thing about Wolfram appearing in 60 games, which was the third-most on the team after Rico Garcia and Yennier Cano, is that he was pretty unmemorable. If you asked me to name the guys in the bullpen, I’d probably get to him after Garcia, Cano, Andrew Kittredge, and Albert Suárez. But he was really a big part of the team! Wolfram made 16 appearances through the team’s first 37 games. His ERA in that span was an unsightly 4.85. It was only 13 innings, so just a blip. But not a good first impression for the season! The 4.85 ERA wasn’t really fair to him, though, as his FIP was a minuscule 0.95. If you’re not as familiar with FIP, it’s a stat that tries to remove defense from the equation when measuring a pitcher’s effectiveness. As you may recall, the Orioles were really bad on defense this year. And if FIP is to be believed, Wolfram was a major victim in the first part of the season. Across those 16 games with mismatched ERA and FIP, Wolfram pitched 13 innings, recording 20 strikeouts and just one walk. He gave up no homers, which is good, but nine extra-base hits, which is bad. His BABIP was .500(!) in that span, so he got very unlucky. I’m singling out his first 16 games because after that, on May 6th, Wolfram went on the Injured List with a lower back strain. Luckily, he needed just the minimum stay to recover and after that was healthy for the rest of the season. Upon his return, Wolfram continued to pitch well without always getting great results in the ERA column. In June he held opposing batters to a .182/.250/.212 hitting line. In July, it was .154/.303/.308. In July, he allowed his first home run of the season. But still, his ERA stayed above 4.00. In June and July combined, Wolfram had a 4.15 ERA. Nearly all of that came in a stretch of three games when Wolfram allowed six runs. Overall, he appeared in 22 games in June and July and allowed zero runs in 18 of those. That’s how Wolfram’s season went for the most part. H

item.title: Alperen Şengün's two-way game, vintage Marcus Smart highlight Houston Rockets' win over Boston Celtics
item.description: Marcus Smart was at his annoying best in pestering his old Celtics squad in the Rockets' win over Boston on Monday night. (Elizabeth Conley/Houston Chronicle) Alperen Şengün wanted one possession to prove himself. For the first chunk of Monday night's contest, the Houston Rockets doubled Boston Celtics star Jayson Tatum whenever Boston brought Şengün into the action. The aggressive defense allowed the Celtics to spray the ball around and get open 3-pointers. At some point in the game, Şengün said he asked coach Ime Udoka for one chance to switch on Tatum and see if he could contain the four-time All-NBA first team selection one-on-one. Rockets guard Marcus Smart, Tatum's former teammate, gave Şengün some backup and Udoka agreed. Şengün held up quite well and the Rockets clamped down on the visiting Celtics in a 109-93 win at Toyota Center. Boston shot just 38.6% from the field and 28.6% from deep. Tatum finished with 19 points but shot 5-for-16 - he added nine assists but with five turnovers, smacking a hand sanitizer stand in frustration as he walked off the court. Jayson Tatum was PISSED after losing to the Rockets 😳 https://t.co/4wWtDCEsLE - BrickCenter (@BrickCenter_) November 3, 2026 Şengün contributed on both ends as the Rockets improved to 7-1. He scored 26 points on 80% shooting and had seven rebounds, ten assists, two steals and two blocks. Only one other center in NBA or BAA history met or exceeded those numbers in a single game: Şengün against Chicago last season , per Sports Reference. "Playing elite basketball," Kevin Durant said. "He's a two-time All-Star, so at this point, it's no surprise to me." Smart's emotional night At Rockets media day, Smart remarked how thankful he was to be on the same side as Durant , getting to watch the superstar forward's shot go in rather than worry about defending him. The feeling is mutual. Durant said after Monday's win that he's happy to have Smart on his team after the veteran guard offered a quintessential Smart performance in a win over his former squad. "Hated playing against him," Durant said, "But I see why everybody loves him as a teammate." Smart drew multiple offensive fouls, performed his signature kip-up to get off the floor, got two steals and, even on an off shooting night, hit back-to-back 3s - sticking double middle fingers into the air after both shots. "Just a lot of pent-up emotions," Smart said of the celebration. "Plus, certain guys on the (Boston) bench was talking … so I let them hear it right back." Smart said "you always want to do good against your former team and show them that you can still go out there and do what you do." Houston Rockets head coach Ime Udoka talks with Houston Rockets forward Kevin Durant (7) during the first half of game action against the Boston Celtics at the Toyota Center in Houston on Monday, Nov. 2, 2026. (Elizabeth Conley/Houston Chronicle) The Durant effect In the second half of the win, Durant and Udoka had a spirited discussion centering arou

item.title: Morning Report | Darren Till reacts to missing out on Jake Paul fight: ‘It’s just a fraudulent show’
item.description: Darren Till | Photo by Ben Roberts Photo/Getty Images Darren Till feels disrespected. On Monday, Jake Paul announced his return to the boxing ring, an eight-round match with MMA fighter and kickboxer Cédric Doumbé on Christmas Eve. The announcement came out of left field as Doumbé never appeared to be on the radar for Paul, and was especially surprising for Till, whose team was negotiating with Paul for the same date. “I thought we were all good to go,” Till told Ariel Helwani . “I’ve been in camp for the past two weeks with me coach. I flew him out, getting ready, seven weeks away, right around the corner. It would’ve been me third fight this year, and a big fight, as well. And out of nowhere, this f*cking daft fight gets announced with Cédric Doumbé. I don’t think anyone outside of his own household even knows who he is. “Jake probably just wants to see how his jaw’s holding up against someone who weighs about 150 pounds on a good day. So, it’s just a fraudulent show. Everyone’s a fraud. Jake’s a fraud. Nakisa[Bidarian, Paul’s business partner] is a little fraud, wasting my time. Couldn’t give a f*ck. Not arsed. If you want to fight me next year, fight me next year. But yeah. I’ve just wasted about 5,000 pounds getting me coach out here for camp and stuff like that, but it doesn’t matter. It’s all good.” This is Paul’s first fight in a year, since getting brutally knocked out by Anthony Joshua in their fight last December. Paul’s jaw was broken in multiple places after that loss and required multiple surgeries to fix, leaving him out of action for an extended period. And Till believes that in his first fight back, Paul simply wasn’t willing to take a risk like fighting him. “Maybe the fight will be there next year, once he tests his jaw against Cédric,” Till said. “Look, Cédric’s a great MMA fighter, but he can’t box, can he really? … “I’m 215 pounds. I’m the same as Jake. I can f*cking hit like f*ck. I’m not slow, I’m fast. I feel like I’m in me prime years. Everyone’s always asking me, ‘Come back to MMA.’ That could be on the cards. Every day I’m feeling better and better. … “So, I’m not bothered. As I said, I’m a fair man. But at the same time, it’s also highly disrespectful, as well. Jake, you’re just a little fraud. You’re just a little f*cking fat goblin.” Till has been chasing a fight with Paul basically since leaving MMA in 2022 to pursue his interests in boxing. That move has been productive for Till, who is 4-0 in boxing, and has also gone 2-0 in BKFC this year. And given his focus on The Sweet Science, Till is adamant that Paul simply doesn’t want the smoke with him. “Jake Paul, he’s a clear, clear juice-head,” Till said. “Look at him, mate, he’s a fat juice-head. There’s a fact for you. Cédric Doumbé’s 170 pounds. I’m not taking anything away from the guy — fantastic MMA fighter and kickboxing career. He’s not a f*cking boxer, mate. I’ve honed my skills for the last three years in boxing with my coach and training alongside all thes

item.title: Kansas City Royals News: Witt named finalist for MVP
item.description: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - SEPTEMBER 26: Bobby Witt Jr. #7 of the Kansas City Royals fields a ground ball during the third inning against the Cleveland Guardians at Kauffman Stadium on September 26, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Jay Biggerstaff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bobby Witt Jr was named a finalist for AL MVP. Witt, 26, joins Tampa Bay Rays third baseman Junior Caminero and Houston Astros designated hitter Yordan Alvarez as finalists. The AL MVP is voted on by the Baseball Writers Association of America. Witt finished second for the 2024 AL MVP. And in 2025, he was fourth behind eventual winner and New York Yankees slugger Aaron Judge. This season, Witt hit .281 with 157 hits, 33 doubles, 18 home runs and 54 RBIs. He also appeared in 143 games while posting a 6.7 WAR (wins above replacement). Perla Paredes at MLB dot com gave an overview of Witt’s case . At the plate, Witt led qualified AL shortstops with a .281 batting average, .441 slugging percentage and 33 doubles. He also finished with 18 home runs, 94 runs scored and 157 hits while posting a .359 on-base percentage and an .800 OPS. Although his offensive numbers were more modest than in previous seasons, Witt showed greater patience at the plate, drawing a career-high 67 walks, surpassing his previous high of 57 in 2024. While Alvarez and Caminero each showcased their power with 42 home runs this season, Witt strengthened his MVP case with his elite defense at shortstop. Carson Roccaforte nabbed a minor league gold glove award . Roccaforte made difficult plays look routine and had a nose for making the spectacular play. The Kansas City Royals’ 2023 Competitive Balance Round B selection logged 320 putouts in the field between two levels, with 13 outfield assists, while posting a perfect 1.000 fielding percentage. Roccaforte, 24, joins Nick Pratto as the only Naturals in club history to claim the honor. Pratto won the award in 2021 with a .998 fielding at first base. Other Naturals who were MiLB Gold Glovers before they reached Northwest Arkansas include INF Michael Massey (2021) and LHP Frank Mozzicato (2024), both of whom achieved the honor with High-A Quad Cities. item.title: The Chicago Bears are a legitimate Super Bowl contender
item.description: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - NOVEMBER 02: Jeffery Simmons #99 of the Chicago Bears celebrates a stop against the Seattle Seahawks during the fourth quarter of the game at Lumen Field on November 02, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Bears picked up a crucial victory on Monday night, defeating the defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks on the road, which is notorious for being one of the toughest places to play in the NFL. They were decisively the better team throughout the evening, picking up a statement 34-17 win in primetime to improve to 6-2 for the season. It was the first game in which All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons suited up for the Bears, and he certainly made his presence felt. But not only did Chicago’s major trade deadline acquisition pay off dividends on Monday, but its offense was also stellar against one of the NFL’s best defenses. Now sitting at 6-2 and firmly in the race for first place in the NFC North, it’s reasonable to think that this Bears roster really has a limitless ceiling. Here are some of my other takeaways from their win over Seattle on Monday. Caleb Williams is special Heading into Monday, no quarterback in the NFL had thrown for over 200 passing yards in a single game against the Seahawks in 2026. Caleb Williams got it done by the third quarter. He was decisive, poised, and accurate against one of the best defenses in the league, throwing for 247 yards, a touchdown, and a 101.0 passer rating. His initial 78.0 grade from the game is enough to keep him ranked No. 6 in the NFL with an 84.0 PFN QB Impact grade so far this season. The Bears felt the pressure from a very talented Seahawks defense, and that loaded Seattle defensive interior made its presence felt on passing downs and in the ground game; D’Andre Swift averaged just 2.6 yards per carry on Monday. Still, Williams maintained his composure, showing off his trademark elusiveness and sack avoidance to extend the play often and create opportunities for Chicago’s offense down the field. This wasn’t Williams’ best statistical performance of the season, but especially given the context of the situation, it was one of his most impressive. Jeffery Simmons was worth the price There was no doubting that Jeffery Simmons was going to be a massive addition to the Bears’ defense when they traded for him on Thursday. The only question was whether he would be worth the massive trade package they gave to the Titans in order to acquire him, which included two first-round draft picks. Simmons showed that he was worth every ounce of that deal on Monday night. He ended the game with six total tackles, two tackles for loss, one pass deflection, one sack, and multiple quarterback pressures. When Simmons got one-on-one opportunities, he rarely lost them, and even when he got double-teamed – which was often – he was still able to make his presence felt. item.title: Falcons Week 8 snap counts from a horrendous loss to the Buccaneers
item.description: TAMPA, FL - NOVEMBER 01: Tampa Bay Buccaneers Quarterback Baker Mayfield (6) scrambles during the regular season game between the Atlanta Falcons and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on November 01, 2026 at Raymond James Stadium in Tampa, Florida.(Photo by Cliff Welch/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The snap counts this week aren’t going to help you feel any better about the game. Sorry about that. Offense QB Michael Penix Jr.: 53 LT Jake Matthews: 53 LG Matthew Bergeron: 53 C Ryan Neuzil: 53 RG Chris Lindstrom: 53 RT Kaleb McGary: 53 WR Drake London: 51 RB Bijan Robinson: 41 WR Jahan Dotson: 38 TE Kyle Pitts: 29 TE Charlie Woerner: 29 WR Olamide Zaccheaus: 25 TE Nick Muse: 10 RB Khalil Herbert: 10 WR Chris Blair: 9 OL Corey Levin: 7 TE Austin Hooper: 7 WR Zachariah Branch: 5 OL Kyle Hinton: 2 If you absolutely have to run and you think trickery or your running back’s guile alone won’t get the job done, bringing on extra offensive linemen is a smart play. The Falcons did roll out Levin on seven snaps and Hinton on a further two to try to bully Tampa Bay’s front, and that largely worked. Levin did a nice job, and had the Falcons committed to running more often, having him out there more often likely would’ve been a smart decision. The Falcons also could’ve leaned more heavily on their usage of Nick Muse alongside Charlie Woerner, given that Muse has proven again and again this season to be a useful blocker. The fact that the Falcons ran the ball 23 times with their two backs and only had Muse and Levin on the field for a combined 17 snaps is, in my opinion, a missed opportunity, given that the only way to beat a run defense as good as Tampa Bay’s is to block as effectively as possible and give Bijan a lane he has a prayer of working with. Bijan still had a couple of special runs in this one—disappearing into the pile and emerging for a first down, for example—but it’s a long season and he needs a bit of breathing room that he wasn’t getting Sunday. That said, the Falcons also threw the ball 24 times (?) in this one and put a third receiver on the field often, so that explains things to some extent. Why they did that on a day where the Bucs threw three passes and the rain made passing treacherous and clearly extremely difficult for Penix is, I think, something I’d like to hear more from Kevin Stefanski and Tommy Rees about this week. item.title: Phillies Infield Castoff Returns To Hated Division Rival After Cut
item.description: CLEARWATER, FLORIDA - MARCH 13, 2026: Christian Cairo #70 of the Philadelphia Phillies runs out a single during the sixth inning of a spring training game against the Baltimore Orioles at BayCare Ballpark on March 13, 2026 in Clearwater, Florida. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) Diamond Images/Getty Images The Philadelphia Phillies enter the offseason with some significant questions about the future of their infield, among several other areas of concern for a team that failed to meet World Series expectations yet again. Franchise shortstop Trea Turner is coming off of the most difficult season of his career, while infield options Alec Bohm, Edmundo Sosa and Luis Arraez are all headed toward free agency. That leaves the organization with several decisions to make as it tries to restructure a roster capable of making another deep postseason run around its incumbent stars. The Phillies will need to determine how much of their current infield group they want to retain and where they can find additional depth. With Turner’s performance prompting questions and multiple familiar names potentially departing, even younger players who have yet to establish themselves in the majors could become important organizational pieces. And now, one such player who once seemed like a promising part of the Phillies’ infield future has returned to one of the team’s biggest rivals. FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Red Sox Longtime Starter Nick Pivetta Cut By New Team After Injury Setback New York Mets Re-Sign Former Philadelphia Phillies Infielder On Monday, the New York Mets announced that infielder Christian Cairo, whom Philadelphia carried on the roster into last year’s spring training, is returning on a big-league deal. “We have signed INF Christian Cairo to a one-year Major League contract,” the Mets announced . The agreement is a big step up for Cairo after he spent the end of this past season in the Mets’ minor league system. The Phillies designated him for assignment on September 13, and New York claimed him off waivers two days later before assigning him to Triple-A Syracuse. The 25-year-old infielder has yet to make his major league debut, but he has drawn interest from multiple organizations as a potential depth option. “Cairo, 25, was Cleveland’s fourth-round pick in 2019 but signed for an overslot bonus just shy of $1MM,” Steve Adams reported for MLB Trade Rumors . “He signed with the Phillies as a minor league free agent this past winter and was added to the 40-man roster at the end of spring training.” FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Dodgers Champion, Former All-Star Joc Pederson Cuts Ties With New Team With $18 Million Move Philadelphia Phillies Infield Faces Questions As Castoff Returns To Division Rival Cairo spent much of 2026 with Triple-A Lehigh Valley, where he hit .227 with a .378 on-base percentage and a .298 slugging percentage, adding four home runs, 35 RBI and 25 stolen bases in 516 plate appearances. item.title: Where will Jonathan Taylor land? Breaking down the Colts’ most likely trade partners
item.description: The Indianapolis Colts have already made it clear that significant changes are coming, trading two of their most accomplished veterans in Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner following the dismissal of general manager Chris Ballard. With the team now sitting at 2-6 after Sunday’s humiliating 42-7 defeat against the Jacksonville Jaguars, attention has increasingly shifted toward the future of another franchise cornerstone: Jonathan Taylor. A little over two weeks ago, I examined Taylor’s hypothetical trade value , projecting that Indianapolis could realistically receive a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 third-round selection in exchange for its star running back. That evaluation came before the Colts began moving key veterans, and with several teams now reportedly expressing serious interest, the market appears to be considerably more competitive than initially anticipated. According to reports from ESPN’s Adam Schefter and NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, Indianapolis has been engaged in trade discussions involving Taylor, with the Denver Broncos, Minnesota Vikings, Seattle Seahawks, New York Giants and Green Bay Packers among the interested teams. Cincinnati has also reportedly entered the conversation, leaving the Colts with several potential trade partners ahead of the November 10 deadline. Perhaps the most important development concerns the asking price. Indianapolis is reportedly seeking compensation comparable to what Carolina received for Christian McCaffrey in 2022, and reports have indicated that the Colts have discussed a package involving a first-round pick and a defensive tackle. While the exact minimum price remains uncertain, I believe it will take a first-round selection, or an exceptional alternative package, to convince Indianapolis to move Taylor. That is a significant investment for a running back, particularly one who will turn 28 next season and is scheduled to earn approximately $34 million over the final two years of his contract. However, Taylor remains one of the league’s best players at his position, and acquiring him would give a contender an immediate offensive centerpiece for the remainder of 2026 and two additional seasons. With just over a week remaining before the deadline, the timing of these discussions is particularly important. Teams aren’t evaluating what their backfields looked like during training camp or even a month ago. Recent performances, injuries, divisional standings and the pressure to win immediately will all influence whether an organization is willing to surrender a premium draft pick. So, which teams actually make the most sense, and where do I believe Taylor will ultimately end up? Denver Broncos Denver has been widely linked to Taylor over the past several days, and there are certainly reasons to understand the interest. The Broncos are 6-2 following Sunday’s crazy 28-24 victory over the Kansas City Chiefs, a result that moved them into first place in the AFC West. With one of the league’s stronger

item.title: Why Arsenal will likely miss out on Como star in January
item.description: Why Arsenal will likely miss out on Como star in January Jacobo Ramon has attracted Arsenal’s attention , with the Gunners considering a move for the Como defender as they look to strengthen their squad. Mikel Arteta wants to maintain the quality of his options and ensure his team remains competitive in the pursuit of major honours. Arsenal currently have one of the strongest squads in European football, and Arteta is aiming to guide them towards further success in the Premier League. They have also impressed in the Champions League over recent seasons, establishing themselves among the competition’s leading sides. The Gunners are determined to keep winning matches and trophies, making the club an attractive destination for players across Europe. However, Ramon may not be convinced that moving to the Emirates would be the best decision for his career at this stage. The defender has impressed at Como, where Cesc Fabregas has helped him develop and establish himself as an important member of the team. His performances have attracted interest from several leading clubs , making him a player whose future could attract considerable attention during the transfer window. Arsenal face a challenge in pursuit of Ramon Arsenal admire the defender and are considering adding him to their squad, but they could struggle to convince him to make the move. Competition for his signature is also expected to be strong, given the reputation he has built through his performances in Italy. According to Football Insider , Ramon believes Arsenal already have a settled defensive unit and may not need another player in his position. That concern could make the Gunners’ pursuit particularly difficult, even if they are prepared to offer him an opportunity to join a club competing for major trophies. (Photo by Gabriele Maltinti/Getty Images) Regular football is central to his decision The report claims Ramon fears that moving to the Emirates could stall his career because he might not receive enough opportunities to play regularly. At this stage of his development, maintaining consistent involvement is important if he wants to continue improving. Although Arsenal can offer a competitive environment and the chance to challenge for major honours, those advantages may not outweigh his concerns about playing time. Arteta would need to explain how the defender fits into his plans and convince him that joining the Gunners would support his development. For now, Ramon’s future remains uncertain, and Arsenal may have to work hard to change his thinking. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ ADMIN COMMENT So here are some simple rules which I must insist commenters follow…. item.description: RALEIGH, NC - NOVEMBER 01: An overhead view as Goaltender Pyotr Kochetkov (52) of the Carolina Hurricanes and Defenseman Shayne Gostisbehere (4) of the Carolina Hurricanes celebrate after the NHL game between the Winnipeg Jets and the Carolina Hurricanes on November 1, 2026 at Lenovo Center in Raleigh, North Carolina. (Photo by Katherine Gawlik/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images First off, Happy Election Day! No matter who you are voting for (and please keep the political opinions out of the comments) if you haven’t already taken advantage of your ability to vote, make your voice heard! One thing you won’t have to worry about if you have to vote later in the day is the start time for the Hurricanes’ game, as the Canes are in central time visiting Nashville for the only time this season. The Predators made news on Sunday by completing a rare one-for-one trade with Seattle. They sent Matthew Wood out to the Pacific Northwest in return for Shane Wright, and all indications are Wright will make his debut against the Hurricanes tonight. There’s a bit of a similar arc playing out with Wright as with another high draft pick that’s playing tonight—Jesperi Kotkaniemi. Both were top five picks in the draft, and both saw early success and then saw a bit of a drop off to the point where they felt a change of scenery was needed. He saw a dip in his goals and overall points last season after a great first full season in 2024-25, but as we all know when you’re a high draft pick and you’ve shown potential, you’ll get multiple chances. Nashville could use the spark—as of today they are just barely out of a wild card spot, which is arguably a stronger position than many felt they would be at the start of the season. That said, they look like they may be this year’s “beneficiaries of the overtime points system.” They’ve only played fourteen games so far and have five overtime losses. Thus, the record looks respectable at 5-4-5 until you realize that means they’ve actually lost nine times. This game is the last of a five game homestand for them, one that started amazingly with a 6-2 thrashing of Colorado, and since then has mirrored the rest of their season with ups—a 5-4 shootout win over Tampa—and downs—a 4-3 shootout loss to the Islanders. One could argue they caught Tampa at the right time considering the atom bomb that was dropped on them as they flew over, but still, you have to win the game. It’s appropriate as the trip to Finland is around the corner that they face the Finnish goalie that they are familiar with: Juuse Saros. He’s played ten of their fourteen games so far, and doing so with a .902 save percentage. The 31 year old netminder looks to be someone who’s going to consider to play what’s becoming “Old school.” He’s going to play the vast majority of the games with only the occasional backup popping in. item.title: Recruiting Roundup: Michigan Football pushing to flip 4-star from SEC school
item.description: Welcome to the Recruiting Roundup, our twice-per-week series breaking down the latest developments on the recruiting trail for the Michigan Wolverines. We’ll keep you up to date on the top targets, the visits they take, the predictions that analysts make, and everything in between. Here’s what you need to know today… Michigan looking to flip four-star Kentucky commit With the end of the 2027 recruiting cycle nearing its end, most players are already committed to a school. That means most of the work at this point is geared towards flipping recruits. One target the Wolverines are eyeing is four-star Kentucky safety commit Tristin Hughes , and he is forming a good relationship with Michigan safeties coach Tyler Stockton. “The bond is steadily increasing, just getting better and better throughout the year,” Hughes told On3’s Ethan McDowell ($) . Hughes is very familiar with Michigan’s rich history, and he knows the program is good at sending defensive guys to the pros. “They’ve produced many NFL-talent guys, and they’re right around the corner,” he said. “Growing up watching them, it’s a great history, a great program, so it’s kind of just me going out and being able to see it.” While visiting earlier this month for the Penn State game, Hughes got a good look at just how good this Michigan defense is. “One of the first things I saw was the stadium,” Hughes said. “I heard the stadium was big, and then I got in there, and it was huge. That was something that was nice. Just getting out there and being able to see their defensive backs go out there and play, create turnovers, get interceptions was another good thing to see.” Michigan is doing a good job staying in the race for the Rocky River, Ohio native, but he is still solid with Kentucky, as he said his commitment to Kentucky is “strong” and that the Wildcats are “like my family there, like my second family.” Ohio State is also pushing hard to flip Hughes. Three-star OT recaps visit, talks Michigan offer 2028 three-star offensive lineman Florians Naglins recently took a visit to Michigan, and it ended with success, as the Wolverines extended an offer to the 6-foot-7, 275-pounder from Northbrook, Illinois. “It was really fun, really good,” Naglins told On3’s McDowell ($) . “Had a wonderful time.” Michigan offensive line coach Jim Harding is the coach who has been recruiting Naglins the most, and they are starting to form a tight bond. “I really like him,” Naglins said. “He’s an amazing guy. He showed a lot of love, showed that he cared.” Like most recruits who visit Ann Arbor, experiencing Michigan Stadium was a highlight during Naglins’ visit. “I liked it a lot,” he said. “The coaches spent a lot of time with you. It was really fun… The Big House is amazing. What a wonderful stadium.” Moving forward, Naglins said he “definitely” plans to return to Michigan for another visit at some point next year. item.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Now that the 2026 season is nearing its halfway point, it’s time to re-evaluate Sportsnaut ’s NFL QB rankings so far. These rankings consider many factors. Most importantly, how did a player perform last week? How does that align with their performance this season? Below, you’ll find out who the NFL’s worst quarterback and the NFL’s best quarterback are, and chances are, you won’t agree with everyone in between either. Related: 1 Trade Candidate For Every Team as NFL Deadline Approaches 32. Daniel Jones, Indianapolis Colts (Last Week: 29) Travis Register-Imagn Images Daniel Jones had already been on a downward spiral coming into Week 8. His confidence didn’t improve after falling to the Jaguars 42-7, getting benched for Anthony Richardson with the game out of hand. But for the second week in a row against a top-10 defense, Jones couldn’t get anything done. He completed 19-of-28 passes for a punchless 144 yards to go with a touchdown and two interceptions while taking three sacks in the process. Last year, Jones was one of the NFL’s best QBs in the first half of the season. This year, he’s been one of the worst. Related: 5 NFL Trades That Could Happen Before Week 9, Including Jonathan Taylor to… 31. Justin Herbert, Los Angeles Chargers (LW: 30) David Butler II-Imagn Images Justin Herbert established an even stronger command over his NFL-leading 10 interceptions by tossing two more in Sunday’s loss, the seventh of the season for the Los Angeles Chargers. Otherwise, he wasn’t too bad, completing 24-of-32 passes for 257 yards, though he also took two sacks for a loss of 26 yards. On a day where the Chargers mustered just 65 rushing yards on 25 attempts, this one isn’t all on Herbert, but as the team’s offensive leader, at some point he needs to put a stop to all the madness.
