item.title: Artemis II commander Reid Wiseman named deputy director for NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory
item.description: null The leader of NASA's first mission around the moon in half a century is the last to announce what's next for him after retiring from active astronaut duty. All four astronauts of the Artemis II mission, which flew around the moon in April, have hung up their spacesuits and moved on to greener pastures. NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), managed by Caltech, announced yesterday that former NASA astronaut Reid Wiseman will step into the role of Caltech associate vice president and deputy director of JPL, beginning Nov. 30. "Reid has spent his career at the edge of what is possible, and he has the technical judgment, operational experience, and leadership to help push that edge farther," NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said in a JPL press release . Wiseman announced his transition to "astronaut emeritus" alongside Artemis II pilot Victor Glover in September. Glover, subsequently, accepted a full-time role as executive advisor to the president of his alma mater , California Polytechnic State University (Cal Poly). Artemis II mission specialists, Christina Koch and Canada's Jeremy Hansen , also made the decision to step away from their spaceflight careers. Hansen announced his career change in July, and has since entered into reservist duty with the Royal Canadian Air Force. Koch, more recently, was appointed as NASA's acting deputy chief engineer, effective Nov. 1. The quartet launched aboard NASA's Orion capsule on April 1, and completed a 10-day flight around the far side of the moon and back. Their mission took them further from Earth than any crewed spaceflight in history, and captured the attention of millions, who were captivated by the astronauts' incredible views and their ability to demonstrate the best traits of humanity, even while being the four people farthest from it. The mission served as a stepping stone in NASA's Artemis program which aims to return astronauts to the surface of the moon and eventually establish a permanent base there. NASA is targeting mid-2027 for Artemis III as a flight test with Orion and the two Artemis lunar lander spacecraft (SpaceX's Starship and Blue Origin's Blue Moon ). If everything goes according to plan, that mission will pave the way for Artemis IV, and the program's first crewed lunar landing in 2028. From left: The Artemis II crew — NASA astronaut Christina Koch, Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen, and NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman and Victor Glover — take time out for a group hug inside the Orion spacecraft on April 6, 2026. (Image credit: NASA) A Baltimore native, Wiseman is a retired U.S. Navy captain who served as an aviator and test pilot before joining NASA's astronaut corps in 2009. He launched to space for the first time on the on the Soyuz TMA-13M mission to the International Space Station (ISS). item.title: Astronauts deploy solar array on 100th US spacewalk by International Space Station crew members
item.description: null Two astronauts successfully installed and deployed the second-to-last upgraded solar array for the International Space Station (ISS) during the 100th U.S. spacewalk from the orbiting outpost. Anil Menon of NASA and Joshua Kutryk of the Canadian Space Agency (CSA), both ISS Expedition 75 crewmates, completed the 7-hour-and-11-minute extravehicular activity (EVA) at 3:08 p.m. EDT (1908 GMT) on Thursday (Oct. 29). The spacewalk began and ended inside the U.S. Quest airlock, with both astronauts wearing NASA's extravehicular mobility unit (EMU) spacesuits. It was the first spacewalk by a Canadian astronaut since April 2019, when David Saint-Jacques ventured into the void with NASA's Anne McClain. NASA astronaut Anil Menon carries a rolled-up solar array to the site where it will be deployed while riding on the end of the Canadarm robotic arm during a spacewalk outside the International Space Station on Thursday, Oct. 29, 2026. (Image credit: NASA) Once outside, Menon and Kutryk worked on unbolting the ISS roll-out solar array ( iROSA ) from a temporary stowage platform. The 10-by-2-by-4-foot (3-by-0.6-by-1.2-meter) rolled-up assembly was delivered to the space station inside the unpressurized trunk of SpaceX 's Dragon cargo capsule earlier this month, on the company's 35th ISS resupply mission for NASA. Menon then secured himself at the end of the Canadarm2 robotic arm and carried the 750-pound (340-kilogram) iROSA to the space station's port side, where he and Kutryk next installed it on the 2A electrical power channel. Kutryk made his way to the worksite along the station's backbone truss. Using bolts to mount the IROSA in place and connecting its electrical cables to tie it into the station's power system (during a night pass, out of safety concerns), the array was ready to be extended. No motor was needed to deploy the iROSA to its 63-foot (19-m) length. The potential energy held by the assembly's rolled-up carbon composite booms was enough to fully unroll the panel. "And we see the iROSA deploying now," reported Mission Control four hours and 23 minutes into the spacewalk. About 12 minutes later, the array had fully extended, draping over about half of the larger but less capable legacy panel on the P4 truss. The station's eight original arrays are showing degraded power output as they have exceeded their 15-year design life. The iROSAs, when used in tandem with their older counterparts, have increased the station's power supply by 20% to 30%. The additional power is needed to support ongoing and planned station operations, including its safe and controlled deorbit , which is currently scheduled for 2030. Having worked ahead of their schedule, Menon and Kutryk removed some of the beams holding the final iROSA in place on its temporary platform and rotated two launch locks that were used in its delivery on Dragon . item.title: 'Crystal Lake' is great, but nothing tops the space horror shenanigans of 'Jason X'
item.description: null Peacock's "Crystal Lake" takes the story of the Voorhees family back to the beginning. It's a full-circle moment revisiting Pamela Voorhees (Linda Cardellini), who's the real star of 1980's "Friday the 13th" and the catalyst for all the murder and mayhem. While it's a welcome shake-up to the timeline of the horror franchise, nothing tops the originality of the slasher-in-space spectacle known as "Jason X". It was 2001, and the "Friday the 13th" franchise had hit a bit of a snag. Audiences had seen Jason Voorhees go everywhere from Crystal Lake to Manhattan and Hell, but where else could this hockey-masked killer go? Screenwriter Todd Farmer had the answer: space . "Jason X" says the quiet part out loud: Jason (Kane Hodder) can't die. In this movie, we find Jason being held at the Crystal Lake Research Facility in 2010. The head of the facility, Rowan LaFontaine (Lexa Doig), wants to put him in a cryogenic chamber, but the government has other plans for him. Things go as well as can be expected, with Jason freeing himself and slaughtering military men like they're pancakes at a buffet. Fortunately, Rowan manages to lure Jason into a cryogenic chamber as he stabs her, leaving them both frozen in time. (Image credit: New Line Cinema / Crystal Lake Entertainment) Fast forward to 2455, when a group of space explorers — led by Professor Brandon Lowe (Jonathan Potts) — discover the research facility and the frozen bodies. They bring Rowan and Jason on board their ship, the Grendel . While they believe Jason to be dead, they're able to revive Rowan using nanotechnology. As it so happens, Jason isn't dead at all (what a shocker); he was just catching up on some sleep and dreaming about stuffing teens in sleeping bags and whacking them against each other. He rises from his slumber and goes on a killing spree in the spaceship. It's not the slasher-in-space concept alone that elevates this flick (it's pretty much a running joke that every horror franchise ends up in space eventually). No, it's the brave (and honestly wild) turns that Jason X takes towards the end. (Image credit: New Line Cinema / Crystal Lake Entertainment) They turn the movie's android KM-14 (played by Lisa Ryder of "Andromeda" fame) into a Rambo-esque action hero in the third act, whereby she annihilates Jason with a combination of hokey martial arts moves and ridiculously overpowered weapons. Sadly, KM-14 makes a critical mistake: she obliterates the silent but violent killer near the medical station where the nanites reside. Not only does Jason get rebuilt bigger and stronger than before, but he's also now a cyborg with a brand-new metal mask and armor. Needless to say, "Jason X" fully commits to every eccentric idea and bonkers premise. From the "Kung Pow"-before-"Kung Pow" face-off between KM-14 and Jason to the totally ludicrous and gory kills that border on implausible, this is the "Friday the 13th" movie that you'd dream up after eating too much cheese at midnight. item.title: Money, Fashion & a Little Attitude! Ayra Starr and Theodora’s “Ms. Paper” Video Has It All
item.description: Ayra Starr wears a pink mini dress and side cap in the official “Ms. Paper” music video. Money, fashion, a little attitude, and Ayra Starr ? Oh, we’re definitely watching! The Starrgirl has just dropped the official music video for “ Ms. Paper ,” her collaboration with French rapper Theodora , and the two are having a lot of fun with this one. Taken from Ayra’s album Starrgirl, the fan-favourite track now has a colourful visual to match its playful lyrics. Produced by The Elements, “Ms. Paper” brings together Afropop rhythms and a catchy mix of English and French as Ayra and Theodora sing about making their own money, enjoying their success, and doing things on their own terms. And with a chorus that goes, “Moi, c’est Miss Kitoko ou Miss Paper,” you can already imagine how much fun the music video was going to be. So, what does being Ms. Paper look like? Apparently, it involves plenty of fashion, money, and a little pop-art fun. The video plays around with currency-inspired graphics, retro magazine covers, and custom toy-box packaging, giving Ayra and Theodora their own colourful world to play in. Ayra appears in a pink mini dress with a matching side cap and cowrie shell details before switching things up in a rich blue halter top, bright red hair, and striking face detailing. And there’s still more to enjoy. Between the money-counting scenes, museum-style portrait frames, and choreography, the video keeps finding new ways to bring the song’s playful mood to life. With Ayra Starr and Theodora moving between languages, fashion, and music, “Ms. Paper” is another fun addition to the Starrgirl era. Watch below The post Money, Fashion & a Little Attitude! item.title: See NASA's Artemis III astronauts meet Trump at the White House as they train for a critical 2027 moon lander test flight (photos)
item.description: null U.S. President Donald Trump just met another NASA Artemis crew. The astronauts of NASA's Artemis III mission visited the Oval Office on Thursday (Oct. 28) and posed for a few photos with the president. Their visit came nearly six months to the day after that of the Artemis II crew, who stopped by the White House on April 29 , 19 days after the end of their historic flight around the moon . President Trump talks to the Artemis III crew on Oct. 28, 2026. (Image credit: The White House) The Artemis III astronauts are NASA's Randy Bresnik (commander), Andre Douglas and Frank Rubio (mission specialists) and the European Space Agency 's Luca Parmitano (pilot). All four — plus backup crewmate Bob Hines of NASA, and agency chief Jared Isaacman — made the White House trip. "It was a great day at the White House with President Trump and the talented crew of Artemis III," Isaacman wrote via X on Thursday . Artemis III will launch to low Earth orbit in the summer of 2027, if all goes according to plan. The roughly two-week-long mission will aim to dock NASA's Orion capsule with SpaceX's Starship vehicle and/or Blue Origin's Blue Moon . NASA selected Starship and Blue Moon to be the crewed lunar landers for the Artemis program , so Artemis III will provide valuable practice : On moon-landing missions, astronauts will launch aboard Orion and then meet up with either Starship or Blue Moon, which will carry them to the lunar surface and back up again. That's slated to happen for the first time on Artemis IV, which NASA plans to launch in 2028 . We don't yet know which private lander(s) will launch on Artemis III; NASA would like to fly both of them, but it's unclear if both will be ready when the time comes. That uncertainty applies to Artemis IV as well. We'll have to wait a bit before we know which spacecraft will have the honor of putting astronauts down on the moon for the first time since Apollo 17 in 1972.

item.title: Cosmic graveyard of zombie planets offers a grisly warning about our own solar system's fate
item.description: null "Sometimes dead is better." Who can forget the immortal words of Jud Crandall, delivered by the incomparable Fred Gwynne in the 1989 film adaptation of Stephen King's Pet Sematary? Turns out Crandall could have been talking about somewhere just as otherworldly as the cursed Chumash burial ground at the heart of one of King's most terrifying works of fiction. That's because astronomers have discovered two husks of two zombie planets shuffling through the gory remains of what was once their planetary neighbors around a long-deceased star, or white dwarf. The shattered planets were revealed by a clear gap in the debris around the white dwarf J1328−1450, located around 1,600 light-years away from Earth. One of the remnants is estimated to be no larger than the size of the average solar system asteroid, while the other is estimated to be between the size of the moon and the dwarf planet Pluto. If this wasn't creepy enough, this haunting planetary system could be a grisly warning about the future of our own solar system after the inevitable death of the sun. White dwarfs like the one at the heart of this system are formed when stars around the same mass as the sun run out of hydrogen in their cores. This means they can no longer fuse hydrogen into helium, the nuclear fusion process that provides the outward push that supports a star against the inward push of its own gravity. As a result, the stars' cores collapse while the outer layers, where nuclear fusion is still proceeding, puff out. This so-called red giant phase can see stars increase their radius by many 100s of times. When it happens to the sun in around 5 billion years, our star will expand to consume the inner planets, including Earth. The red giant phase ends when the outer layers disperse along with the wreckage of consumed planets, leaving a smoldering stellar core, now a white dwarf, surrounded by the disk-shaped remains of its outer layers and cannibalized planetary children. But this may not be the final death of all the planets that once orbited the now-dead star. "We have known for some time that planets may survive beyond the transformation of their central star, but this is the first example of a complex system with a double debris disc and potentially two surviving planetesimals," research leader Nicola Gentille Fusillo, an astronomer at the Università degli Studi di Trieste, Italy, said in a statement. Violent stellar death can't kill these two planetary Jason Voorhees This system differs from others seen because of the large gap between the remarkably stable inner and outer rings. All previously known debris discs around white dwarfs have been surrounded by single, flat, rotating disks, not a double structure like this. "The system is a rare glimpse of the violent, chaotic process by which a planetary system meets its end, and it hints that dead stars can have disc structures far more complex than previously realized," team member Gentle Fusillo of the Astronomical Observat

item.title: AWIEF and Open Society Foundations Champion Women-Led Enterprises for Peace and Security in Africa at AWIEF 2026
item.description: The Africa Women Innovation and Entrepreneurship Forum (AWIEF) is pleased to announce its partnership with Open Society Foundations (OSF) for AWIEF 2026 , taking place on 10 and 11 November 2026 at the Cape Town International Convention Centre (CTICC). The annual AWIEF Conference, currently in its twelfth edition, is a flagship convening of entrepreneurs, investors, corporates, government, and development partners from across Africa and beyond. The partnership will take center stage during the opening plenary, Peace Dividends: Why Women-Led Enterprise Is a Security Strategy, Not Just an Economic One , exploring how women entrepreneurs contribute to economic stability, rebuild trust in communities affected by conflict, and help create the foundations for lasting peace. Across fragile and post-conflict regions, from the Sahel to the Great Lakes and the Horn of Africa, women entrepreneurs play a vital role in restoring livelihoods and rebuilding local markets. Yet their contribution to peace building and security remains overlooked and unsung. The plenary will examine how women-led businesses can strengthen community resilience, alongside the need for more effective access to capital, supportive policies and funding systems that empower their role in peace and development. Opening Plenary: Peace Dividends The discussion will be moderated by Idil Absiaye, Regional Head of Women, Peace and Security (WPS) Policy at UN Women , and feature: Aimée Ongeso , Program Manager, Transformative Peace, Open Society Foundations. Ibrahim Mulushewa Eshete , Co-Founder and Executive Director, Center for National and Regional Integration Studies (CeNRIS), Ethiopia. Amb. Ninikanwa O. Okey-Uche, Consul General, Consulate General of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, Johannesburg. Yvette Mwanza, CEO of Kivu Mineral Resources and President of the North Kivu Chamber of Mines, Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). Bringing together perspectives from peace building, regional integration, diplomacy and business, the panel will explore what is working on the ground and what needs to change to better support women-led enterprises as contributors to peace and security. Through this partnership, AWIEF and OSF will spotlight the connection between women’s economic empowerment, resilient communities and sustainable peace, reinforcing the importance of recognizing women entrepreneurs as not only drivers of economic growth, but also contributors to stability across Africa. The opening plenary takes place on 10 November 2026 at the CTICC, Cape Town, as part of AWIEF 2026. item.title: Big cats, unexplained lights and a floodlit eclipse — 7 skywatching 'horror stories' to keep you entertained this Halloween
item.description: null Halloween is almost upon us! To celebrate we've pulled together a series of short "skywatching horror stories" perfect for getting you in the mood for the spooky season. Granted, stargazing may not be the most hazardous of past times. But you'd be surprised how often things can go wrong. The best laid plans can be shattered by the unforeseen, unexpected phenomena can leave you scared witless, or mother nature itself can step in to remind us how little control we have over the environment around us. Many of the stories serve as a cautionary tale, while others are simply..unfortunate. Be sure to share your stories of skywatching "horror stories" in the comments below for a chance to feature in next year's Halloween coverage! An unexplained light show over France And how better to kick off our Halloween skywatching tales than with a retelling of the strange event that terrified my entire family during a trip to France, two decades ago. We had rented a house in the Charente, with few neighbors and no city lights. It was a stargazer's paradise, so each night we would sit outside as dusk's light faded to twilight. One night, we stood transfixed as an electrical storm conjured sheet lightning in the distance, when without warning a shining ball of light burst into being on the near horizon. We watched, unsettled as the yellow-red light gently descended behind a row of oaks before passing over the nearby field. An artists depiction of the path taken by ball lightning during a sighting in 1902 near the city of Nice, France. (Image credit: Universal History Archive/Universal Images Group via Getty Images) My mom fled inside, convinced that we'd seen a UFO , while my dad and brothers stood and watched as the light silently flitted between the trees before disappearing from sight around five minutes after it had appeared. We were alone in the darkness, trying to make sense of what we'd seen when a rustle in the bushes had us borderline sprinting inside, all pretences of bravery gone and images of alien greys in our heads. It was almost certainly a boar. Our best guess is that we saw some kind of rare electrical phenomenon that night, like ball lightning , which has been reported over 10,000 times throughout recorded history but is still very poorly understood. My mom maintains that we narrowly avoided being abducted. Total(ity) disaster Our next entry comes from Space.com's Skywatching Editor Daisy Dobrijevic, who traveled all the way from the U.K. to the U.S. in the hope of seeing her first total solar eclipse , only to have totality ruined by a series of extremely unfortunate events! "My first-ever total solar eclipse experience in Rochester, New York, on April 8, 2024 , was memorable for all the wrong reasons, Dobrijovic explained. "I was attending the Rochester Museum & Science Center's ROC the Eclipse Festival, where thick clouds had completely obscured the sun . But even without seeing the eclipse itself, totality was extraordinary. An ominous dar

item.title: Tunji Olowolafe Charts Three Strategies for Research Excellence at OAU at 65
item.description: At the Obafemi Awolowo University (OAU), Ile-Ife 65th anniversary celebration, Dr. Tunji Olowolafe , Founder of the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation (TOF) , called on Nigerian universities to open research to more people, test long-held beliefs with scientific rigour and carry discoveries out of the laboratory and into the economy. Speaking on the theme, Promoting Research Excellence and Innovation in Postgraduate Studies: Charting the Future, Dr. Olowolafe reframed research as the disciplined habit of correcting a nation’s course based on evidence. He described the postgraduate college as the intellectual engine room of a nation, where society sends its sharpest minds to challenge conventional wisdom and demand honest, data-driven answers. His first strategy called for opening the gates of research earlier, wider and more flexibly. He urged OAU to make its Staff Schools benchmarks for Africa, with science, technology and artificial intelligence at the core of the curriculum. He pointed to the Foundation’s Gbemisola Olowolafe Memorial Community Secondary School in Are-Ekiti, which opened in September 2025 with 100 students and now has more than 170, alongside an ICT centre teaching artificial intelligence, coding, graphic design and Mandarin, with instructors teaching live from Beijing through a Starlink connection. “The postgraduate researchers of 2040 are sitting in primary classrooms today,” he said. He also questioned whether every road to postgraduate research must run through a four-year degree, inviting universities to recognize prior learning and demonstrated expertise without lowering standards. With only about one million of the two million UTME candidates admitted in 2025, he argued that flexible, digital study must become the standard model, since a digital campus needs no physical acreage. This builds on the Foundation’s Project Digi-Teach, which is training academic staff at Ekiti State University (EKSU) for digital proficiency. His second strategy urged researchers to test what society believes. Rather than dismissing indigenous knowledge without investigation or defending it without validation, he called for rigorous testing, citing Chinese scientist Tu Youyou , whose study of a centuries-old herbal remedy produced the malaria treatment artemisinin and a Nobel Prize. He extended the same principle to national history, including sensitive chapters such as the Civil War. “She neither rejected tradition nor accepted it. She tested it,” he said. The third strategy focused on pushing research out of the laboratory and directly into the economy. Dr. Olowolafe advocated university promotion structures that reward patents, commercial products and solved industrial problems alongside traditional journal publications. “Research is complete only when it leaves the laboratory and improves lives,” he said. Pointing to OAU’s exceptional tech pedigree, including Flutterwave and Moniepoint founded by its graduates, he challenged the global alumni commu

item.title: The universe in the eye of a telescope | Space photo of the day for Oct. 29, 2026
item.description: null The Swedish-ESO Submillimetre Telescope reflects the stars at the La Silla Observatory in Chile. (Image credit: J. Rodrigues/ESO) Stars shine in the vast aluminum dish of the Swedish-ESO Submillimetre Telescope (SEST) in this photograph captured by astronomer and astrophotographer José Rodrigues during a recent visit to the European Southern Observatory's La Silla Observatory in Chile. What is it? Rodrigues' image captures "airglow" infusing the night sky over La Silla with a soft orange glow, which is created as sunlight interacts with molecules in the upper atmosphere, according to the University of Lancaster . The subtle phenomenon can be seen reflected in the 15-meter (49-foot) primary dish of the SEST telescope along with the myriad stars of the Southern Hemisphere, as the dome of the ESO's 3.6-meter telescope looms in the background. Why is it incredible? "Despite knowing about its 15-meter diameter beforehand, I was amazed by its size," Rodrigues noted in the ESO image release. The SEST first opened its great eye to the universe in 1987, at which time it was the only large telescope in the Southern Hemisphere tasked with collecting submillimeter wavelengths of light that exist beyond the visible light spectrum. These specific wavelengths of light are emitted by wandering comets and colossal clouds of cold molecular dust and gas threaded throughout the Milky Way and beyond. SEST's observations improved our knowledge of ancient galaxies, star formation and so much more, with its perch 2,375 meters (7,792 feet) above sea level granting it a near unrivalled view of the heavens above. The SEST telescope was decommissioned in 2003, though its work was continued by the more capable Atacama Pathfinder Experiment (APEX) and the Atacama Large Millimeter/Submillimeter Array (ALMA). With its working days over, the SEST telescope now stands as a quiet mirror reflecting the stars of the Southern Hemisphere night sky, seemingly pondering mysteries of the universe that it once tried to solve

item.title: SpaceX fires up Starship upper stage ahead of landmark Flight 15 test launch (video)
item.description: null SpaceX just checked another big box on the path to its 15th Starship test flight, which promises to be pretty epic. The company conducted static-fire tests with Starship 's Ship upper stage on Monday (Oct. 26) and Tuesday (Oct. 27), igniting its Raptor engines while the vehicle, known as Ship 42, remained anchored to the ground. "Ship 42 static fires complete. The Starship preparing for Flight 15 performed a full duration, six-engine static fire, and fired a single Raptor engine to simulate a deorbit burn," SpaceX said in a Wednesday (Oct. 28) X post that shared video of the tests. SpaceX conducts a six-engine static fire test with its Flight 15 Starship upper stage on Oct. 27, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) The Ship 42 tests come on the heels of a successful 33-engine static fire with Booster 22 , the Starship Super Heavy first stage that will conduct Flight 15. Everything therefore appears to remain on track for Flight 15, which SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk has said is targeted for sometime in November. All Starship launches are worth watching, but this one should be particularly exciting. Musk said last week that SpaceX will try to catch both Ship and Super Heavy during Flight 15, provided the company can get regulatory approval to do so. These catches are performed by the "chopstick" arms of the launch tower at Starbase, SpaceX's Starship launch and manufacturing hub in South Texas. The company has snagged Super Heavy on three Starship test flights to date but has not yet attempted a Ship capture. Double chopstick catches will be the norm on operational Starship launches, if all goes to plan. This recovery strategy will reduce the time needed to get Super Heavy and Ship ready for reflight, significantly boosting launch cadences, according to SpaceX. (Starship is designed to be fully reusable, unlike SpaceX's Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy rockets, whose upper stages are expendable.) SpaceX is already riding a historic success with Starship: The megarocket reached orbit for the first time ever on Flight 14 , which took place on Sept. 28. And Ship deployed 26 of the company's next-gen Starlink V3 satellites during that flight, starting the assembly of a new broadband constellation that Musk has said will eventually consist of 100,000 spacecraft . Starlink V3 missions will therefore make up a significant percentage of Starship launches for the foreseeable future. But SpaceX also plans to use the megarocket to build an even bigger constellation in Earth orbit — Starmind , which could harbor one million of the company's AI data center satellites.

item.title: Stunning solar eclipse photos reveal giant hole and mysterious 'smoke rings' in the sun's atmosphere
item.description:
Tereza is a London-based science and technology journalist, aspiring fiction writer and amateur gymnast. Originally from Prague, the Czech Republic, she spent the first seven years of her career working as a reporter, script-writer and presenter for various TV programmes of the Czech Public Service Television. She later took a career break to pursue further education and added a Master's in Science from the International Space University, France, to her Bachelor's in Journalism and Master's in Cultural Anthropology from Prague's Charles University. She worked as a reporter at the Engineering and Technology magazine, freelanced for a range of publications including Live Science, Space.com, Professional Engineering, Via Satellite and Space News and served as a maternity cover science editor at the European Space Agency.

Newly released photographs of the sun captured during the Aug. 12 total solar eclipse reveal the sun's outer atmosphere in unprecedented detail. The images, released by researchers working as part of the Solar Wind Sherpas project coordinated by the University of Hawaii, also show rare structures in the solar wind known as smoke rings. Named for their resemblance to the circles blown by smokers, these vortices were first identified in solar eclipse photographs captured in 2008. The researchers had long struggled to explain the processes behind their formation. They now know the rings are a result of the temperature differences in the coronal plasma and spread along the sun 's magnetic lines deep into interplanetary space. "This year, we have managed to capture those smoke rings really well," Miloslav Druckmüller, a professor of mathematics at the Brno University of Technology in the Czech Republic, who leads the image processing efforts for the Solar Wind Sherpas Team, said in a statement . "They are beautifully twisted vortices and there are very many of them in the corona." The images, taken from the Pico Trigaza mountain in Spain, also reveal a giant coronal hole — an opening in the sun's magnetic field lines — through which solar wind can escape more readily at very high speeds of up to 500 miles per second (800 kilometers per second). Coronal holes are cooler regions in the sun's atmosphere that appear darker in extreme ultraviolet and X-ray images taken by probes in space. They form in regions where the sun's magnetic field lines extend outward into space rather than looping back to the surface, allowing high-speed solar wind to escape. These structures can persist for weeks or even months. High-res images of the sun taken during the total solar eclipse of August 2026 reveal a coronal hole and intriguing structures known as smoke rings in the solar corona. Click the right arrow for an annotated version. item.title: Night Plane review – join the jumbo jet to hell in this indie horror head trip
item.description: Liquid Static Studio; PC You take on the role of flight attendant in this clever and absorbing retro-style game that veers from daft horror spoof to genuinely disturbing There was always something creepy about the job-simulator genre. All those mindless automatons queueing up to use your bus, bar or bed store, or whatever workplace you are trapped in for the duration of the game. The endless repetitive tasks. The emptiness of the world beyond your corporate existence. Together, these elements scream existential terror … which is perhaps why we are now seeing a new indie sub-genre of job sim horror games, including Home Safety Hotline, Dredge and more recently, Grease Trap ’99, a Lovecraftian mystery set in a Scottish chip shop. Now, we have Night Plane, in which you take on the role of a flight attendant on a jumbo jet to hell. It all starts kind of normally. You turn up for the first day of your new job, meet your colleagues, then take your spot at the departure gate, checking in customers and being careful to root out anyone with invalid tickets. Once on the plane, you roll your trolley down the aisle, serving booze and inedible meals, and occasionally dealing with passenger complaints. Then the plane crashes and, frankly, it all goes downhill from there. Continue reading...

item.title: SpaceX's Starfall capsule delivers cargo for US Air Force in landmark 'point to point' space mission
item.description: null The U.S. Air Force is opening up about the SpaceX Starfall cargo capsule it flew on a recent rideshare mission to orbit — and showing off what the capsule carried. The Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) completed a point-to-point rocket cargo delivery test using the secretive uncrewed reentry vehicle, confirming on social media its recovery of the package in the Pacific Ocean. "With support from SpaceX , the AFRL agile cargo pods were recovered after splashdown," the AFRL wrote in an X post on Oct. 26. The Starfall capsule launched on a Falcon 9 rocket as a part of SpaceX's Bandwagon-5 mission, which lifted off from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station on Oct. 20 . Starfall carried a number of AFRL-developed cargo pods designed to transport military equipment through space and back to Earth . The successful recovery of the pods marks a big step forward in the Air Force's effort to examine the viability of point-to-point (P2D) rocket cargo missions. "This was a critical achievement to demonstrate the potential of Rocket Cargo delivery for point-to-point rapid global mobility for the Future Force," said AFRL Technology Transition Office director Adam Remaly in a press release on Oct. 20. Photos included in the AFRL social media post show military personnel unpacking a recovered cargo pod for inspection. Each pod contained sensors to monitor temperature conditions through launch, reentry and splashdown, as well as to measure the shock and vibration forces exerted on its cargo. For its first Starfall mission, AFRL packed its cargo pods with representative items like medical equipment, food ration packs and other military kit that might be helpful for surviving an emergency somewhere that's tough to reach via conventional transportation. To that end, AFRL said it also conducted a fit check of a UNI-PAC III life raft inside Starfall, which could potentially be included in future tests. With support from SpaceX, the AFRL agile cargo pods were recovered after splashdown in the Pacific Ocean. AFRL Each pod contained representative mission equipment to study the effects of temperature, shock, and vibration of the cargo environments during launch and reentry. AFRL With support from @SpaceX, the AFRL agile cargo pods were recovered after splashdown in the Pacific Ocean. Each pod contained representative mission equipment to study the effects of temperature, shock, and vibration of the cargo environments during launch and reentry. #Readiness https://t.co/yWoND13ur4 October 26, 2026 "Researchers paid special attention to the electronics equipment and survival gear, including a SATCOM-enabled tracker, batteries, a reverse osmosis desalinator, survival gear and emergency medical equipment," AFRL said in its release. item.title: On this day in space! Oct. 28, 1971: Britain launches its 1st satellite Prospero into space on a Black Arrow rocket
item.description: null On Oct. 28, 1971, the United Kingdom launched its first satellite. The satellite was named Prospero, but it was also known as the X-3. This wasn't Britain's first satellite , but it was the first and only one the British space program launched with one of its own rockets. The first six British satellites all launched from the United States on NASA rockets. Prospero launched on a carrier rocket called the Black Arrow. The Prospero mission was the fourth and final flight of a Black Arrow rocket . Prospero was designed to study how the environment in space affects communications satellites. It tested things solar cells and telemetry systems, and even had a micrometeoroid detector that would determine small particles in space posed a threat to the spacecraft. The mission lifted off from the Woomera Range Complex in Australia. While the launch was a success, the rocket's final stage bumped into the satellite after it separated, and the collision broke one of Prospero's four radio antennas. But the satellite still worked, and it remained operational until 1973. The satellite Prospero X-3 is launched from the RAAF test range in Woomera, South Australia, by a British Black Arrow carrier rocket, 28th October 1971. Central Press/Hulton Archive/Getty Images Britain developed the Black Arrow as its national satellite launcher. Based on the smaller Black Knight research rocket this was a three-stage vehicle, 12.87m tall. SSPL/Getty Images Why it mattered The launch of Prospero is etched in the history books of British spaceflight. To this date, it remains the first and last British satellite ever launched on a native rocket built in the United Kingdom. The 66-kilogram satellite launched on a three-stage Black Arrow R-3 rocket and flew in an elliptical orbit that ranged between 522 km to 1,300 km above the Earth. The rocket itself was based on the smaller Black Knight research rocket and stood nearly 13 meters tall. While the launch was successful, the Black Arrow program, which had seen two failures and two successes, was ultimately canceled. The research satellite Prospero is the only British spacecraft to launch on the British-built Black Arrow rocket. (Image credit: Wikimedia Commons/Geni) The Prospero satellite, meanwhile, operated in orbit for two years, with regular communications ending in 1973, though it was contacted at least once each year through 1996, according to the BBC . The satellite remains in orbit today, its legacy such that at least one company - the Scotland-based space startup Skyrora, has announced plans to retrieve Prospero in orbit and deorbit in Earth's atmosphere. That Skyrora plan, announced in 2021 , would use the company's space tug to rendezvous with the defunct Prospero, latch onto it and pull it from space. The company aims to launch its Skyrora XL rocket out of a Saxavord Spaceport in Scotland. item.title: 5 days beneath the waves: What it's like to live in an underwater 'space station'
item.description:
Dr. Michaela Musilova is an award-winning astrobiologist, explorer, professional speaker and author. Michaela has been conducting space-related research at institutions around the world, including NASA, ESA, CalTech, the Canada-France-Hawaii telescope and many others. She was the Commander of 40 simulated missions to the Moon and Mars — the most missions led to date.

Currently, Michaela is the President and Founder of the nonprofit XtremeFrontiers. She is pioneering a unique global project: Astro Seven Summits. It's a world-first in combining expeditions to the highest mountain on each continent with scientific research in collaboration with NASA and institutions worldwide, educational activities and filming documentaries.

Michaela is also a consultant for numerous companies across the globe for topics ranging from Mars missions all the way to museum exhibitions, such as for the Smithsonian. She is one of very few people to have ever led research projects on all seven continents.

Michaela’s work has been recognized through numerous awards, such as Forbes 30 Under 30, Top 100 Women in Aerospace and Aviation, and the Emerging Space Leaders Grant.

Michaela is regularly invited to give keynote presentations and performs a variety of outreach activities globally as a science communicator. She has been giving interviews to international media for over 20 years, writing scientific and educational articles, and she co-authored her biography, "Woman from Mars."

Living underwater was surprisingly peaceful. It was in many ways exactly what I imagine living on Mars would be like one day. There were no humans around us, except for my three SEA STAR crewmembers and me. Apart from the human noises we made, we couldn't hear anything other than the life support systems keeping us alive submerged 22 feet (7 meters) below the surface. We were living in these extreme conditions to study the challenges astronauts may face on long-duration space missions. Since performing research in space is still rare and expensive, there are numerous facilities around the world that focus on recreating space-like conditions on Earth . One of those stations is the Jules' Undersea Lab, where the SEA STAR simulated space mission took place. This underwater habitat was called "La Chalupa" when it was built in the 1970s. Its purpose was to allow divers to live and perform research as aquanauts — people who spend more than 24 hours underwater in a so-called state of saturation. Today, the Jules' Undersea Lab is located near Key Largo, in Florida. However, it was originally designed to be mobile — inside a barge 20 feet wide and 60 feet long (6 to 18 meters). The SEA STAR crew inside the Jules' Undersea Lab, as seen from the outside of the station by a member of Mission Control. Presented at the National Theatre, Lagos, the installation placed local craftsmanship at the centre of a contemporary African living experience. Deep burgundy surfaces, raw tree bark, sculptural textures and a contemporary sofa from S.EA.HOMES created a setting shaped by Nigerian culture and heritage. Guests could handle samples and discover the possibilities behind the finished spaces. Wireless headphones offered a choice of music and the founder’s statement, while a digital screen introduced the firm’s services, products, and projects. An in-house photographer captured visitors engaging with the installation, making their presence part of its story. Through this approach, S.EA.CONSULTING made a clear statement: African exhibitions should give local makers, materials and ways of living a central role. The experience connected interior architecture with sourcing, craftsmanship and everyday life, demonstrating how collaboration transforms individual products into spaces with meaning. For S.EA.CONSULTING, showing the world how we live begins with recognising the value of what we make, the stories we carry and the hands that bring our ideas to life. Rooted in culture. item.title: ISS astronaut will conduct Canada's 1st spacewalk in 7 years on Oct. 29: Watch it live
item.description: null The next International Space Station (ISS) spacewalk will have more maple-leaf flavor than usual, as a Canadian astronaut will become the first to go outside the orbiting complex in seven years. Canadian Space Agency (CSA) astronaut Joshua Kutryk, who's also a colonel in the Royal Canadian Air Force, will help the ISS boost its power supply during his first-ever spacewalk on Thursday (Oct. 29). Kutryk will be joined by NASA astronaut Anil Menon, who has done three spacewalks already and also serves as a colonel with the U.S. Space Force . The duo are scheduled to venture outside the orbiting lab at 8 a.m. EDT (1200 GMT), kicking off a spacewalk that will last roughly 6 hours and 45 minutes. You can watch it live here at Space.com , courtesy of NASA, beginning at 6:30 a.m. EDT (1030 GMT). Official photo of Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk. (Image credit: Canadian Space Agency) It will be the first of two extravehicular activities (EVAs) for Menon and Kutryk, with the second expected to occur no sooner than Nov. 5. During the two spacewalks, the astronauts will deploy the seventh and eighth International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Arrays (iROSAs). iROSAs lie on top of the existing, decades-old arrays on ISS, which are naturally degrading with age. The first iROSA rolled out in 2021. Once all eight are installed and running, the station will see its power supply rise from 160 kilowatts to about 215 kilowatts — a boost of roughly 30%. A Canadian capcom, too The capcom (capsule communicator) for both spacewalks will be CSA astronaut Jenni Gibbons. She has experience in this role already, serving as a capcom on NASA's Artemis II mission around the moon this past April. And she'll serve as lead capcom for Artemis III , which will test crewed lunar landers in Earth orbit next summer , if all goes to plan. Also helping Kutryk and Menon will be Canadian space technology, specifically Canadarm2 — the ISS robotic arm tasked for spacewalk support, among other maintenance duties. "It's been busy preparing for the upcoming spacewalks," Menon said about Canadarm2 in a Saturday (Oct. 24) X post . Ground controllers recently moved the arm over to the "trunk" or storage area of a SpaceX Dragon cargo spacecraft, which brought the two iROSA arrays up earlier this month .Canadarm2 picked up the IROSAs and moved them to a transporter for the astronauts. "It even loosened bolts for us before the spacewalks … I'm grateful for the help," Menon added. During the Oct. 29 spacewalk, Canadarm2 will do even more. Kutryk and Menon will slide an array off its transport rail and then have Menon get onto a Canadarm2 platform, to put the array into his hands. From inside the ISS, NASA astronauts Luke Delaney and Jessica Watkins will carefully move Canadarm2 to put Menon and the array at the ISS port-installation site, supporting the 2A electrical-power channel. Each array is about 10 feet (3 meters) long when folded up and weighs 750 pounds (340 kilograms) here

item.title: Meet Apeiron, Virgin Galactic's 1st 'Delta-class' space plane
item.description: null Virgin Galactic has officially unveiled the first space plane in its next-gen "Delta" line, and announced the results of the worldwide vote to choose its name. Spaceship Apeiron will be the first Delta-class vehicle, Virgin Galactic revealed on Wednesday (Oct. 28). Apeiron (pronounced "A'-per-on," according to the announcement) takes its name from the ancient Greek word meaning "boundless," and was selected through a public poll that drew votes from thousands of people across 83 countries and six continents. The reveal comes on the same day that the space plane is scheduled to be flown from its manufacturing facility in Mesa, Arizona, to Spaceport America in New Mexico, where the vehicle will undergo final preparations before beginning flight tests. Apeiron was one of four finalist names that Virgin Galactic narrowed down from a list of 276 employee-submitted suggestions. After the public weighed in, Apeiron came out on top over Horizon, Explorer and Ascend. “Apeiron, the Boundless, captures the ambition of human spaceflight and the possibilities it opens for humanity," Virgin Galactic CEO Michael Golglazier said in a company statement. "The extraordinary response to the public vote made choosing this name even more meaningful." The shiny new space plane will be attached to Virgin Galactic's VMS Eve carrier aircraft for its journey to Spaceport America, where engineers will complete work on its avionics software ahead of Apeiron's first flight tests and eventual operational missions. The new Delta-class vehicle replaces Virgin's earlier space plane model, VSS Unity , which flew seven suborbital missions during its operational lifetime between the summers of 2023 and 2024. The company suspended VSS Unity flights to focus efforts on Apeiron's development, and now hopes to begin flying customers again in mid-2027. Each Delta-class vehicle is equipped to accommodate up to six passengers. (Image credit: Virgin Galactic) Once they're in regular operation, Virgin plans to fly each of its Delta-class vehicles as many as eight times a month. A second Delta-class space plane is already under construction and is expected to join Apeiron at Spaceport America around the same time that Virgin restarts flying passengers, about 675 of whom are still waiting in line with tickets for a seat on one of the company's suborbital jaunts, according to the company's Q2 2026 SEC filing . Now, more than 100 of those future space travelers are beginning their initial preparations for flight, with more ticketholders expected to follow once Virgin brings the second Delta-class vehicle into service. When the company began selling seats aboard its space plane in 2014, when VSS Unity was still under construction, tickets were priced around $200,000. Today, that price has jumped to $850,000 per seat, according to a report by Latte . item.title: Social media is full of weird video game mashups. Where are they all coming from?
item.description: AI tools are making it easier to modify and recreate games, raising questions about piracy, copyright and how far the technology could disrupt the industry • Don’t get Pushing Buttons delivered to your inbox? Sign up here If your social media algorithms have clocked that you’re into video games, something strange will have happened in the past few weeks. Your feed, like mine, will have been full of clips of streamers playing bizarre mashups of popular video games . Skyrim in Minecraft. Halo, except the main character is Mario. Skate 2 in Call of Duty maps. A flood of professional-looking fan-coded game mods that are mildly interesting to look at for 30 seconds, but ultimately inconsequential. Would I download a mod that lets me play Wii Bowling inside a zombie shooter? No, but I am very interested in where they came from. Of course, the answer – or at least, most of the answer – is AI. After a week of researching this (thanks especially to Replay Mode on YouTube for this informative video , which set me down this track) I now understand that these mashup mods are not just AI-generated videos, but AI-assisted coding. Basically, as of a few weeks ago, Anthropic’s Claude has become extremely good at decompiling video game code. Games are written by humans in readable code and then compiled into binary 1s and 0s that the PC or console running it can read; decompiling is the reversal of that process, revealing a game’s source code, which humans can then edit and mess around with for fun. This used to be an extremely laborious process. But now it is not, because humans aren’t doing much of it any more. Continue reading...

item.title: Eko Hotels at 50: A Defining Moment for African Hospitality on the Global Stage
item.description: The Legacy Gala & Awards night : Fifty Years of Building More Than a Hotel. Fifty Years of Building a Nation’s Hospitality Identity. 2nd of October 2026 was written in the sands of time, because some hotels are built to accommodate history, others are built to make it. For fifty years, Eko Hotels & Suites has done both. Beneath the lights of an extraordinary golden jubilee celebration, one of Africa’s most recognisable hospitality institutions made a statement that extended far beyond the walls of the magnificent Eko Convention Centre . Africa does not lack the capacity to deliver world-class excellence. What it needs are more institutions courageous enough to demonstrate it. The occasion was The Legacy Gala & Awards night, the grand celebration marking fifty years of Eko Hotels & Suites. An evening of African grandeur, international entertainment, cultural pride, distinguished personalities and extraordinary hospitality. But to describe it simply as a glamorous anniversary celebration would be to misunderstand its significance. This was not merely a party, It was fifty years of enterprise taking a bow, Fifty years of memories finding their voices, Fifty years of an institution reminding a continent that excellence is not foreign to Africa a nd for one unforgettable evening, history took attendance. A Hotel Became Part of a Nation’s Story There are buildings that occupy space, and there are institutions that occupy memory, Eko Hotels & Suites belongs to the latter. Across five decades, its corridors have welcomed presidents and policymakers, entrepreneurs and entertainers, diplomats and dreamers, international visitors and generations of Nigerian families. Within its halls, businesses have been negotiated, friendships formed, cultures celebrated, careers launched and milestones immortalized. For many, Eko Hotels is where Lagos welcomes the world, f or others, it is where the world first encounters the warmth, ambition, sophistication and extraordinary possibilities of Lagos. Yet perhaps its greatest achievement is not simply that it has remained standing for fifty years. It is that it has remained RELEVANT. In a world where brands disappear as quickly as trends emerge, longevity is an achievement. But longevity accompanied by reinvention is leadership. Eko Hotels has consistently demonstrated that hospitality must evolve beyond accommodation, It must become an experience, a cultural encounter, a n economic opportunity, a reason to travel and reason to return. Because the greatest hotels do not merely sell rooms. They give destinations a reputation worth travelling for. The Night Africa Wore Her Crown The Legacy Gala & Awards night brought together more than 1,000 distinguished guests, representing an extraordinary convergence of business, government, entertainment, culture and society. Among the dignitaries were Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu , Deputy Governor Dr. Kadri Obafemi Hamzat , prominent business leaders, industry executives, ce

item.title: Yinka Ogunbiyi Shows HaloBraid’s Automated Hair-Braiding Technology in New Demo
item.description: Harvard graduate Yinka Ogunbiyi, creator of the automated HaloBraid device engineered to complete braids up to five times faster. What if you could get your braids done in a fraction of the usual time and still leave the salon with the style you wanted? A new demonstration of HaloBraid, the automated braiding device created by Nigerian-American engineer and Harvard graduate Yinka Ogunbiyi , gives us a closer look at how that could work. Designed to help professional hairdressers braid hair up to five times faster while reducing the physical strain that comes with hours of styling, HaloBraid is now being demonstrated in action. And the interesting part is that the machine doesn’t do everything. The stylist still plays an important role in the process. Here’s how it works. The stylist sections the hair, applies the necessary products and starts the braid by hand before feeding it into the device. HaloBraid then handles the repetitive weaving along the length of the hair, while the stylist returns to finish and seal the ends. This means the machine takes care of a time-consuming part of the process, with the stylist still responsible for creating the final hairstyle. For Yinka, the idea behind HaloBraid comes from a very personal experience. Sharing the story behind the invention, she said: My braid story starts at age four, sitting between my mum’s legs as she braided my hair for the first time. Since then, I’ve spent thousands of hours getting my hair braided — and heard the same story from stylists and clients again and again: braiding is beautiful, but it takes too much time and too much strain. As a biomechanical engineer, I knew there had to be a better way, so we built HaloBraid with stylists from the beginning, bringing together inventors, designers, and builders behind some of the world’s most loved hair and beauty products. HaloBraid was built for my mum, my stylists, my aunties, and people around the world who know what it means to spend hours in the chair. The company has also secured $7 million in seed funding, with the investment round led by Seven Seven Six, the venture capital firm founded by Reddit co-founder Alexis Ohanian , who is married to tennis champion Serena Williams . With the newly shared demonstration, HaloBraid is showing how its technology works alongside professional stylists, combining hand-braiding techniques with automated weaving to reduce the time and physical effort involved in protective hairstyling. item.title: How Can Africans Advance Cross-Country Equity and Opportunities Through AI?
item.description: Photo source: Goalkeepers 2026 Report For years, Africans have explored how to connect seamlessly without hurdles. As several opportunities are being explored through AI, Africans are also exploring whether AI can be used to advance cross-country opportunities and equity. If it can, what would it look like? What are the initial challenges that can hinder it from happening? What can governments and organisations do to enhance it? Artificial intelligence is changing how people learn, work, build businesses and access information. For young Africans, what opportunities does it present to solve problems, develop new skills and participate in an economy that is becoming increasingly digital? How can those opportunities be available to everyone in the same way? A young person with reliable internet access, a laptop and access to AI training has an advantage over someone who lacks these resources. The gap widens further when we consider young people across countries with different levels of digital infrastructure and investment. If AI is to improve the lives of African youth, access to its benefits must extend beyond the countries and communities already positioned to take advantage of it. African countries need to work together, share resources and invest in solutions that respond to the needs of their people. Bill Gates in Rwanda. Photo by Jean Biziman for Gates Foundation One area, and perhaps the most important area, where this cooperation matters is language. There are thousands of languages spoken in Africa. But much of the technology used to develop AI relies on data in widely spoken languages (in many cases in Africa, English and French), leaving many African languages underrepresented. This limits who can use these tools and how useful they can be. For a young person who speaks an African language but struggles with English or French, AI may not offer the same opportunities it offers someone who is fluent in these languages. The Masakhane research community is working to address this problem by developing natural language processing technologies for African languages. The community consists of Africans representing different languages across Africa. It is an example of what can happen when African researchers collaborate to make technology more inclusive. Through initiatives such as the Masakhane AI Languages Hub, researchers can develop datasets across 40 African languages to support the creation of more useful AI tools. In the 2026 Goalkeepers Report , Bill Gates said AI must b e able to work in every language spoken to create significant equality. Goalkeepers 2026 Report African countries can build on this work by investing in shared language resources, supporting local researchers and making datasets available for responsible use. Instead of each country working independently on similar challenges, regional partnerships could help researchers share knowledge and develop tools that serve communities across borders. item.title: Taiwo Awoniyi Honoured with ‘Beyond the Pitch’ Award at the 2026 Best of Africa Awards in London
item.description: Taiwo Awoniyi posing on the red carpet at the Best of Africa Awards 2026 in London. Nigerian international striker Taiwo Awoniyi has picked up the prestigious ‘Beyond the Pitch’ Award at the 2026 Best of Africa Awards in London, marking a major moment of recognition for his work both on and off the football field. Known for his clinical goalscoring ability and strength upfront, the Nottingham Forest and Super Eagles forward plays as a central striker at the highest level of European football. Beyond his professional career in the English Premier League, Taiwo has consistently directed his resources towards community development, healthcare support, and youth empowerment in Nigeria—most notably through his funding and sponsorship of the Kwara Kiddies League, an initiative providing structured grassroots football opportunities for young talents in Kwara State. The Best of Africa Awards, held annually in London, celebrate the outstanding contributions of African figures and individuals of African heritage across sports, entertainment, and social impact. Supported by the Professional Footballers’ Association (PFA), the ‘Beyond the Pitch’ accolade specifically highlights athletes who use their global platform to drive tangible social change and uplift their home communities. Taking to Instagram to reflect on the honour, Taiwo shared a message with his followers: Life can give you so much, but what truly matters is what you choose to do with what you’ve been given. Grateful to receive the PFA Beyond the Pitch Award at the Best of Africa Awards 2026. His philanthropic commitments include fully funding the annual Kwara Kiddies League tournament, providing kits, equipment, and cash prizes for grassroots teams across Ilorin and surrounding areas to help young footballers build sustainable career pathways. Through City of Cities: Where Taste Rules , Heineken will celebrate the people, cultures and creative expressions shaping Lagos, bringing its presence to life across the Heineken Lounge, Heineken Runway Showcase, Heineken Studio and the After Party. First introduced in Lagos in 2025, City of Cities: Where Taste Rules celebrates the diversity that defines the city, where different cultures, styles, communities and perspectives converge. From fashion and music to food, art and social experiences, Lagos draws its character from the people and influences that shape it. For Heineken, this reflects the many ways taste is expressed, experienced and shared. Over the past decade, Heineken’s partnership with Lagos Fashion Week has evolved through initiatives that explore the relationship between fashion, craftsmanship and taste. From the sustainable fashion focus of Woven Threads in 2022 and the Dyelab collaboration in 2023 to the H45 Collection in 2024 and the introduction of City of Cities: Where Taste Rules in 2025, each chapter has offered a distinct expression of the partnership. In 2026, Heineken continues this legacy, creating new opportunities to connect with the people, ideas and experiences shaping contemporary Nigerian fashion and culture. This year’s Heineken Lagos Fashion Week theme, CRAFTED , provides a natural context for this next chapter, celebrating intentionality, artistry, craftsmanship and more considered approaches to fashion and sustainability. Reflecting this spirit, Heineken will bring its presence to life across the week through the Heineken Lounge, the Cruise Collection runway, Heineken Studio and the Heineken Studio After Party, creating experiences that extend beyond the runway. Making its Nigerian debut, Heineken Studio introduces a new dimension to the brand’s exploration of taste and innovation. Described as Heineken’s Playground of Innovation, Studio explores new ways to serve and experience lager through experimentation, brewer expertise and discovery. Experiences such as Foam Infusions will invite guests to discover unexpected flavour combinations, bringing a fresh perspective to taste within the wider Heineken Lagos Fashion Week experience. Bringing together Jameson’s Irish heritage and the unmistakable Naija spirit of Port Harcourt, the event offered guests different ways to connect with the brand, discover its story and enjoy a weekend of entertainment, creativity and shared experiences. Across all three days, whiskey education remained an important part of the experience, giving guests insight into Jameson’s heritage and craftsmanship. Food and fashion also added to the atmosphere, allowing guests to enjoy different aspects of the gathering while connecting with one another. Each day featured a distinct experience, delivered in partnership with communities and platforms that brought their own energy and expertise to the programme. Day One: Skating, Music and Energy with Plus2.34 and Voltage District The experience opened with a celebration of skating, music and creative expression in partnership with Plus2.34 and Voltage District. The two communities brought their connection to skating and music to the event, creating a lively atmosphere where guests could watch the skaters in action, enjoy live performances and connect through shared interests. The day’s entertainment featured performances by Sons of Ubuntu, Black Dave, WeAreAllChemicals and Ifeme, alongside DJ sets that kept the energy going. Guests also took part in interactive games, adding friendly competition to the opening day’s programme. Day Two: Games, Competition and Good Music with Game Fiesta Day two brought a playful and competitive atmosphere dubbed “Play City” through Game Fiesta, which turned familiar games into opportunities for guests to interact, compete and have fun together. Guests had different ways to participate, challenge their friends and enjoy the experience beyond the music. Music was another major highlight of the day, with Peruzzi delivering a standout performance. DJ Kaydee, DJ Faithful and DJ Diamond took to the decks, while Hypeman Mayor and Pandora kept the atmosphere lively. Real Chuksy and Annie Drumz added to the day’s entertainment, bringing together live music, DJ sets and games for an engaging Jameson experience. Day Three: Water Games and Entertainment with Whetlvnd The final day introduced a different kind of fun through Whetlvnd, which brought its waterpark-inspired experience to Jameson Distillery. Guests enjoyed water-based games and splashing activities, providing a refreshing change of pace and an opportunity to round off the three-day experience with friends. item.title: Lagos Fashion Week 2026 Kicks Off Today! Dates, Venue, Designers & What to Wear
item.description: Lagos Fashion Week street style features showing tiered ruffles, tailored white co-ords, and structured Aso-Oke dresses. Clear your schedules and start ironing out those statement fits— Lagos Fashion Week 2026 officially starts today! From Wednesday, 28th October to Sunday, 1st November 2026, the fashion capital of Africa transforms into a high-energy hub of runway shows, street style spectacles, and creative exchanges. Organised by Style House Files, Africa’s premier fashion platform is back to connect local designers, international buyers, media, and style lovers from across the globe. The theme for the 2026 season is “CRAFTED: Heritage. Innovation. Circular Futures.” This year focuses heavily on pushing sustainable, locally rooted craft straight into the global spotlight. Through initiatives like Green Access and the Fashion Business Series, the event highlights zero-waste tailoring, circular design, and modern interpretations of traditional African textiles—from handwoven Aso-Oke and Akwete to indigo-dyed Adire. Whether you are pulling up to the tents in person or following every outfit update online, this complete guide breaks down everything happening this season—from venue details and designer expectations to the street style cues you need to know. When and Where Official Dates: Wednesday, 28th October – Sunday, 1st November 2026 Primary Venue: The LagosFW Tents, Federal Palace Hotel, Ahmadu Bello Way, Victoria Island, Lagos, Nigeria Opening Night: The official Welcome Party kicks off tonight, Wednesday, 28th October Main Runway Shows: Thursday, 29th October – Saturday, 31st October at the Federal Palace Hotel Closing Showcase: Offsite presentations across select cultural spots in Lagos on Sunday, 1st November What to Expect on the Runway Expect five days packed with rich storytelling, structured silhouettes, and bold textile work. Runway mainstays like Lisa Folawiyo , Andrea Iyamah , Ejiro Amos Tafiri , Ugo Monye , Fruché , and Abiola Olusola will be delivering season-defining moments alongside coveted labels like Christie Brown , Cute Saint , Bloke , and Emmy Kasbit . Meanwhile, the Green Access cohort will present sustainable, forward-thinking mini-collections that show how the next generation of African designers is tackling circular fashion. Rather than standard catwalks, several offsite and tent presentations will also showcase raw fabric production, live artisan weaving, and intricate beadwork. Street Style Cues and What to Wear The pavement outside the LagosFW Tents is just as important as the runway inside. Street style stars, content creators,and fashion editors bring their absolute best to Victoria Island. If you are putting your looks together, consider these three styling cues: Reimagined Heritage Fabrics: Think tailored suits, co-ord sets, or corsets cut directly from Aso-Oke or Adire. item.title: Tiwa Savage Is Giving Rock-Chic Glamour in Black Latex and Purple Fur
item.description: Tiwa Savage posing in a royal purple fur coat layered over a black latex catsuit. A glossy black catsuit and a purple fur coat? Tiwa Savage says she knows how to make both work, and work perfectly! And looking at her latest outfit, we have absolutely no reason to argue. The Afrobeats superstar stepped out in a figure-hugging black latex catsuit with a plunging V-neckline, throwing a plush, oversized royal purple fur coat over the look. Because when you’re Tiwa Savage, why settle for one fashion statement when you can make two? And can we talk about the accessories? Chunky gold bangles stacked on her wrists, sculptural gold earrings and a razor-sharp black bob that gave the entire look an extra dose of attitude. Between the glossy latex, the rich purple fur and those bold gold pieces, Tiwa had every detail working in her favour. Tiwa Savage styling a black latex catsuit with a royal purple fur coat and gold hardware. Now, here’s something to borrow from Tiwa’s style book. A fitted catsuit already does a lot for your silhouette, so pairing it with an oversized coat gives the outfit a completely different shape. That contrast between something sleek and something voluminous is what makes the combination so interesting. And rather than reaching for barely-there jewellery, take Tiwa’s approach with chunky metallic pieces that can hold their own against the outfit. Tiwa Savage backstage wearing a black latex catsuit and gold earrings There’s also a little colour lesson here. Black and purple make a gorgeous pairing, particularly when you play around with textures. The shine of the latex against the softness of the fur makes both colours look even richer, while the gold accessories add warmth to the overall look. So, the next time you’re putting together an all-black outfit and wondering what could give it a little extra personality, you might want to take a page out of Tiwa Savage’s book. Tiwa Savage highlighting her purple fur jacket, gold bangles, and glossy makeup. *** Photo Credit: Tiwa Savage/Instagram The post Tiwa Savage Is Giving Rock-Chic Glamour in Black Latex and Purple Fur appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. item.title: Cynthia Erivo & Ayoade Bamgboye Take “Wicked” to LagOz in Hilarious SNL UK Sketch
item.description: Cynthia Erivo and Ayoade Bamgboye posing through traditional beaded door curtains on the set of Nigerian Wicked. If you thought you’d seen every possible spin on Wicked, think again. West End and Broadway royalty Cynthia Erivo recently stepped onto the Saturday Night Live UK (SNL UK) stage to deliver a masterclass in comedy—teaming up with Ayoade Bamgboye to reimagine the magical land of Oz as a chaotic, low-budget Nollywood blockbuster. Titled “ Nigerian Wicked “ and presented by the fictional Holy Ghost Productions (the satirical masterminds behind classic titles like Beyonce’s Revenge and Light Skin, Dark Heart ), the viral sketch is a love letter to Nollywood tropes complete with a gloriously stressful sound mix. In this universe , Elphaba (played with maximum green-paint intensity by Ayoade Bamgboye) and Glinda (brought to life by Cynthia Erivo in a pink tracksuit, blonde wig, and matching cap) are sharing a room stacked with vintage trunk luggage. Their relationship is wonderfully tense , highlighted by an unforgettable moment where Glinda casually slaps Elphaba because she is “very classless” , only for Elphaba to complain that the room smells like egg. Ayoade Bamgboye as Elphaba and Cynthia Erivo as Glinda sitting on set during the Nigerian Wicked sketch on Saturday Night Live UK. Things get even wilder when the duo boards a train to the land of LagOz to see The Wizard (played by Hammed Animashaun ) , who turns out to be completely broke, rocking a “No-lex” watch instead of a Rolex, and offering his guests some off Bailey’s Irish Cream. While Elphaba is simply hoping her magical transformation defies gravity and earns her a “skinny BBL”, Glinda is laser-focused on her ultimate priority: getting her hands on a Birkin bag. Complete with flying monkeys , Professor Goat , dramatic musical interludes , and a full, gloriously long credit sequence introducing Cynthia by her full traditional name— Cynthia Onyedinmanasu Chinasaokwu Owezuke Amarachukwu Echeumuna Erivo ——this sketch is pure comedic gold from start to finish. Watch below *** Photo Credit: Matt Crockett/Instagram The post Cynthia Erivo & Ayoade Bamgboye Take “Wicked” to LagOz in Hilarious SNL UK Sketch appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. item.title: MSS Event Tech Academy: Graduates Over 60 Students Building a New Generation of Event Technology Professionals
item.description: Mobile Screens and Sound Limited (MSS) , a leading event technology and production company, in partnership with KolaDaisi University, has graduated over 60 students from the inaugral MSS Event Tech Academy, marking a significant milestone in the company’s commitment to developing skilled professionals for Nigeria’s growing events and entertainment industry. The graduating students completed a 10-week intensive training programme across one of six specialised departments: LED Screen Engineering; Sound Engineering; Camera Craft and Video Production; Light Design and Control; Event Management and Production; and Rigging and Trussing. Speaking at the graduation ceremony, Tunbosun Kola-Daisi , Managing Director of Mobile Screens and Sound Limited, encouraged the graduates to view the milestone as the beginning of their continued professional development. “Graduation should not be seen as the end of learning, but as the beginning of a lifelong journey of growth. The event technology industry continues to evolve, and as technology advances, so must our knowledge, creativity and capacity to adapt. I encourage every one of our graduates to remain curious, keep learning, and continue to sharpen their craft. We are proud of what you have achieved, but we are even more excited about what you will go on to become.” Held at Darlington Hall in Lagos on Tuesday, September 29, the ceremony also served as a practical demonstration of the technical and practical skills acquired throughout the academy. The graduates took responsibility for the event’s technical and production delivery, including event management, LED screens, sound, lighting and camera operations, giving them the opportunity to apply their skills in a live production environment. In recognition of outstanding performance, the five best graduating students will receive employment opportunities with MSS, providing them with a direct pathway into the event technology industry. Prof. Olajumoke Morenikeji , Vice-Chancellor of KolaDaisi University, highlighted the importance of initiatives that connect education with the realities of the professional world. She remarked, “At KolaDaisi University, we believe strongly that the university must remain connected to the realities of the world beyond the classroom. Education must prepare our students not just to seek employment, but also to create value, solve problems, and create opportunities for themselves. This is why initiatives like the MSS Event Tech Academy are important.” The inaugural Academy comes as MSS prepares to mark its 20th anniversary in October, following two decades of work across Nigeria’s event technology and production landscape. During this period, the company has built expertise across the technical and creative disciplines required to deliver major events and live experiences, while contributing to the growth and professionalisation of the sector.
